# Introduction {#sec-intro}

For the same eight fictitious startups as in Study 3 (**Servora**, **Curato**, **Ironhall**, **Foliant**, **Pulsegrid**, **Paperloom**, **Sentyl**, and **Axonmesh**), we ran an online experiment in which we varied what participants were told about the visual design of the pitch decks. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three instruction conditions (control, disclosure, and disclosure plus explanation) in a 1:5:2 ratio. Before reviewing the pitch decks, they read one of the following messages:

- **Control**: *"You will review four startup pitch decks and at the end distribute 100 units of investment capital across them. Please review each pitch deck and judge the venture from the venture information presented."*
- **Disclosure**: *"You will review four startup pitch decks and at the end distribute 100 units of investment capital across them. The visual design of the decks was created by a design agency for this study. The founders did not create or choose it. The design tells you nothing about the ventures or their founders. Please review each pitch deck and judge each venture from the venture information presented."*
- **Disclosure plus explanation**: the disclosure message with two additional sentences before its final sentence: *"You will review four startup pitch decks and at the end distribute 100 units of investment capital across them. The visual design of the decks was created by a design agency for this study. The founders did not create or choose it. The design tells you nothing about the ventures or their founders. Visual design can make the same information feel easier or harder to process. That feeling is not evidence about the venture. Please review each pitch deck and judge each venture from the venture information presented."*

After the message, participants answered two comprehension questions about it (in the control condition, about the logistics of the study). A wrong answer led to a notice and a repeated presentation of the message (up to three attempts). After the second pitch deck, participants saw a short reminder of their message.

The experiment was incentive-compatible: at the end, participants distributed 100 units of investment capital across the four startups they had reviewed, one startup was drawn with a probability proportional to its allocation, and the participant received a bonus of up to £1.00 that was proportional to the substantive quality of this startup (its q-score, as rated by an independent panel of seven large language models, cf. the [LLM Ratings Reproducibility Report](Detailed_Report_2_LLM_Ratings.qmd)). Since the high and the low fluency version of a pitch deck had the same q-score, the bonus rewarded substantive quality only. The q-scores and the individual ratings of the language models are available in the [online repository](https://researchbox.org/1836&PEER_REVIEW_passcode=NKVZFU). Participants who answered the comprehension question about the bonus incorrectly twice were screened out during the study and compensated for their time.

Each participant reviewed four of the eight startups, one pitch deck for each combination of visual fluency (low vs. high) and substantive quality (low vs. high), resulting in a 3 (instruction condition; between-subjects) x 2 (visual fluency; within-subjects) x 2 (substantive quality; within-subjects) design. Sixteen rotation patterns counterbalanced which startups a participant saw and in which version. Before and after the reminder, participants saw one high and one low fluency pitch deck each, in random order. There was no time limit. After each pitch deck, participants answered a factual question about the startup (factual recovery). After the investment allocation, they answered questions about the study's purpose and indicated how much the visual design had told them about the startups' quality and the founders' competence (beliefs). Finally, participants saw each pitch deck again and rated it with respect to how easy it had been to study (processing ease; called *felt ease* in the preregistration) and the startup's potential irrespective of the pitch deck's visual design (perceived venture quality, the main dependent variable). @fig-procedure summarizes the procedure.

We ran the experiment on [Qualtrics](https://www.qualtrics.com), where the pitch decks were displayed as slide images in a click-through viewer, and recruited the participants via [Prolific](https://www.prolific.co). For details, see the corresponding [AsPredicted](https://aspredicted.org) preregistration listed in @tbl-prereg.

As this report is dynamically created with R and Quarto, we also report all code.
However, for readability, code is hidden by default and only the relevant results are shown.

```{r}
# preregistered equivalence bound for H2 (in rating points)
eq_bound <- 0.225


# Custom functions
#
# negate %in%
`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)
#
# position of each block in a Qualtrics "Display Order" string
# -Note: the input are the *_DO columns, so the string might look like
#        "FeltEaseSlot3|FeltEaseSlot1|FeltEaseSlot4|FeltEaseSlot2"
display_position <- function(x, labels) {
  parts <- stringr::str_split(x, stringr::fixed("|"))
  out <- vapply(
    parts,
    function(p) {
      if (length(p) != length(labels) | anyNA(p) | anyDuplicated(p) > 0) {
        return(rep(NA, length(labels)))
      }
      match(labels, p)
    },
    integer(length(labels))
  )
  out <- as.data.frame(t(out))
  names(out) <- labels
  out
}
#
# total time spent viewing a deck (in seconds)
# -Note: the raw string holds the 14 per-slide viewing times in deciseconds
#        (i.e., tenths of a second), separated by "|"
viewtime_sec <- function(x){
  vapply(stringr::str_split(x, stringr::fixed("|")),
         function(p) sum(as.numeric(p)) / 10, numeric(1))
}
#
# number of slides viewed (i.e., the leading number of the coverage string,
# e.g., "7/14" -> 7)
slides_seen <- function(x){
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(x, "^\\d+"))
}
#
# all 14 slide images of a deck loaded without failure (i.e., "14/14;fail=0")
images_ok <- function(x){
  stringr::str_extract(x, "^\\d+") %in% as.character(14) &
    stringr::str_extract(x, "(?<=fail=)\\d+") %in% "0"
}
#
# extract the results of a one-sample t-test of a participant-level contrast
# against zero and Cohen's d_z and put the results together as a table
# -Note: NAs (i.e., participants with at least one invalid deck) are removed
#        before the test. The 95% confidence interval is always two-sided.
contrast_tbl <- function(x, alternative = "two.sided", ...){
  # remove missing values
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  # perform t-test
  tres <- t.test(x, mu = 0, alternative = alternative)
  # perform two-sided t-test to get the (two-sided) 95% confidence interval
  cres <- t.test(x, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided")
  # construct p-value
  pval <- ifelse(tres$p.value < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(tres$p.value, 3))
  # construct return df
  df <- data.frame(N = length(x), Mean = NA, SD = NA, CI = NA, test_statistic = NA, p = NA, d = NA)
  # fill values
  df$Mean <- weights::rd(mean(x), 2)
  df$SD <- weights::rd(sd(x), 3)
  df$CI <- paste0("[", weights::rd(cres$conf.int[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(cres$conf.int[2], 2), "]")
  df$test_statistic <- paste0("t(", tres$parameter, ") = ", sprintf('%.2f', tres$statistic))
  df$p <- pval
  df$d <- weights::rd(mean(x) / sd(x), 2)
  return(df)
}
#
# format a Bayes factor (values above 1,000 in scientific notation,
# e.g., 4.37 × 10^7)
bf_fmt <- function(bf){
  ifelse(bf > 1000,
         paste0(sprintf('%.2f', bf / 10^floor(log10(bf))), " × 10<sup>", floor(log10(bf)), "</sup>"),
         sprintf('%.2f', bf))
}
#
# verbal interpretation of a Bayes factor BF10 (classification of Lee &
# Wagenmakers, 2013, adapted from Jeffreys, 1961) and a table note that
# explains it
bf_label <- function(bf){
  dplyr::case_when(bf > 100 ~ "extreme evidence for the alternative hypothesis",
                   bf > 30 ~ "very strong evidence for the alternative hypothesis",
                   bf > 10 ~ "strong evidence for the alternative hypothesis",
                   bf > 3 ~ "moderate evidence for the alternative hypothesis",
                   bf > 1 ~ "anecdotal evidence for the alternative hypothesis",
                   bf == 1 ~ "no evidence for either hypothesis",
                   bf > 1/3 ~ "anecdotal evidence for the null hypothesis",
                   bf > 1/10 ~ "moderate evidence for the null hypothesis",
                   bf > 1/30 ~ "strong evidence for the null hypothesis",
                   bf > 1/100 ~ "very strong evidence for the null hypothesis",
                   TRUE ~ "extreme evidence for the null hypothesis")
}
bf_note <- function(bf, alternative){
  paste0("BF<sub>10</sub> = ", bf_fmt(bf), " indicates ", bf_label(bf),
         " (classification of Lee & Wagenmakers, 2013). That is, the data are ",
         ifelse(bf >= 1, scales::comma(signif(bf, 3)), scales::comma(signif(1 / bf, 3))),
         " times more likely under ", ifelse(bf >= 1, paste0("the alternative hypothesis (", alternative, ")"),
                                             "the null hypothesis (no effect)"),
         " than under ", ifelse(bf >= 1, "the null hypothesis (no effect).",
                                paste0("the alternative hypothesis (", alternative, ").")))
}
#
# extract the results of a Welch two-sample t-test and Cohen's d and put the
# results together as a table
# -Note: Cohen's d uses the average of the two variances as the standardizer
#        (since the Welch test does not assume equal variances)
welch_tbl <- function(x, y, alternative = "two.sided", ...){
  # remove missing values
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  # perform Welch t-test
  tres <- t.test(x, y, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)
  # construct p-value
  pval <- ifelse(tres$p.value < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(tres$p.value, 3))
  # construct return df
  df <- data.frame(N_1 = length(x), N_2 = length(y), Mean_1 = NA, Mean_2 = NA,
                   test_statistic = NA, p = NA, d = NA)
  # fill values
  df$Mean_1 <- weights::rd(mean(x), 2)
  df$Mean_2 <- weights::rd(mean(y), 2)
  df$test_statistic <- paste0("t(", weights::rd(tres$parameter, 1), ") = ", sprintf('%.2f', tres$statistic))
  df$p <- pval
  df$d <- weights::rd((mean(x) - mean(y)) / sqrt((var(x) + var(y)) / 2), 2)
  return(df)
}
#
# extract the results of an equivalence test (two one-sided tests, TOST) of a
# participant-level contrast against the bounds -bound and +bound and put the
# results together as a table
# -Note: equivalence is concluded if both one-sided tests are significant at
#        alpha = .05, which is the same as the 90% CI lying inside the bounds
tost_tbl <- function(x, bound = eq_bound, ...){
  # remove missing values
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  # perform the two one-sided tests
  res_lower <- t.test(x, mu = -bound, alternative = "greater")
  res_upper <- t.test(x, mu = bound, alternative = "less")
  # construct p-values
  p_lower <- ifelse(res_lower$p.value < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(res_lower$p.value, 3))
  p_upper <- ifelse(res_upper$p.value < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(res_upper$p.value, 3))
  # construct return df
  df <- data.frame(test = c(paste0("Lower bound: mean > -", bound), paste0("Upper bound: mean < +", bound)),
                   test_statistic = c(paste0("t(", res_lower$parameter, ") = ", sprintf('%.2f', res_lower$statistic)),
                                      paste0("t(", res_upper$parameter, ") = ", sprintf('%.2f', res_upper$statistic))),
                   p = c(p_lower, p_upper))
  return(df)
}
#
# preregistered decision rule for H2 (steps applied in the preregistered order)
# -Note: x = fluency contrast in the disclosure condition,
#        x_control = fluency contrast in the control condition
h2_decision <- function(x, x_control, bound = eq_bound){
  # remove missing values
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  x_control <- x_control[!is.na(x_control)]
  # estimate and two-sided test against zero
  est <- mean(x)
  p_zero <- t.test(x, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value
  sig_negative <- p_zero < .05 & est < 0
  sig_positive <- p_zero < .05 & est > 0
  # equivalence test (TOST)
  p_lower <- t.test(x, mu = -bound, alternative = "greater")$p.value
  p_upper <- t.test(x, mu = bound, alternative = "less")$p.value
  equivalence <- p_lower < .05 & p_upper < .05
  # control vs. disclosure (Welch t-test, two-sided): control effect higher?
  p_comparison <- t.test(x_control, x, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value
  control_higher <- p_comparison < .05 & mean(x_control) > est
  # decision rule
  if (sig_negative & est <= -bound) {
    return("(1) significantly negative with the estimate at or beyond the bound: overcorrection")
  }
  if (sig_positive & est >= bound) {
    return("(2) significantly positive with the estimate at least 0.225: persistence supported")
  }
  if (equivalence & control_higher) {
    if (sig_positive) return("(3) switched off (a significantly positive effect remains inside the bound)")
    if (sig_negative) return("(3) switched off (a significantly negative effect remains inside the bound)")
    return("(3) switched off")
  }
  if (sig_positive & est < bound & !equivalence) {
    return("(4) significantly positive below 0.225 without passing equivalence: reduced but present")
  }
  return("(5) indeterminate")
}
#
# step number and outcome of the decision rule for H2, taken from the text that
# `h2_decision` returns (e.g., "(2) significantly positive ...: H2 supported"
# -> step 2, outcome "prediction supported")
h2_step <- function(decision){
  as.integer(stringr::str_extract(decision, "(?<=^\\()\\d"))
}
h2_outcome <- function(decision){
  outcome <- stringr::str_remove(stringr::str_remove(decision, "^\\(\\d\\) "), "^.*: ")
  stringr::str_replace(outcome, "H2 ", "prediction ")
}
#
# summarize a manipulation check: observed number of ratings, mean, and SD per
# condition (high, low) and the test of the manipulated factor in a
# mixed-effects model (from `lmerTest::lmer`, effect coding, random intercepts
# for participants and startups) and put the results together as a table
# -Note: Cohen's d is the model-based difference between the high and the low
#        condition (i.e., two times the coefficient) divided by the square root
#        of the sum of all variance components (Westfall et al., 2014).
#        p-values are based on Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom.
mc_tbl <- function(model, effect, y, group, outcome){
  # observed values per condition
  n <- c(sum(group == "high"), sum(group == "low"))
  m <- c(mean(y[group == "high"]), mean(y[group == "low"]))
  sdv <- c(sd(y[group == "high"]), sd(y[group == "low"]))
  # test of the manipulated factor
  fe <- coef(summary(model))[effect, ]
  pval <- ifelse(fe["Pr(>|t|)"] < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(fe["Pr(>|t|)"], 3))
  # standardized effect size
  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model))
  d_es <- 2 * fe["Estimate"] / sqrt(sum(vc$vcov))
  # construct return df
  return(data.frame(DV = c(outcome, ""), condition = c("high", "low"),
                    N = scales::comma(n), Mean = weights::rd(m, 2), SD = weights::rd(sdv, 3),
                    test_statistic = c(paste0("t(", scales::comma(unname(fe["df"]), accuracy = .1), ") = ",
                                              sprintf('%.2f', fe["t value"])), ""),
                    p = c(unname(pval), ""), d = c(weights::rd(unname(d_es), 2), ""),
                    row.names = NULL))
}
#
# summarize factual recovery: observed number of answers and share of correct
# answers per fluency condition (high, low) and the fluency effect in a mixed
# logistic regression (from `lme4::glmer`, effect coding) and put the results
# together as a table
# -Note: with effect coding, the odds ratio (high vs. low) is exp(2 * coefficient)
recovery_tbl <- function(model, y, group){
  # observed values per condition
  n <- c(sum(group == "high"), sum(group == "low"))
  share <- c(mean(y[group == "high"]), mean(y[group == "low"]))
  # fluency effect
  fe <- coef(summary(model))["fluency1", ]
  pval <- ifelse(fe["Pr(>|z|)"] < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(fe["Pr(>|z|)"], 3))
  # construct return df
  return(data.frame(DV = c("Correct answer", ""), condition = c("high", "low"),
                    N = scales::comma(n), share = sprintf('%.1f', 100 * share),
                    test_statistic = c(paste0("z = ", sprintf('%.2f', fe["z value"])), ""),
                    p = c(unname(pval), ""), or = c(sprintf('%.2f', exp(2 * fe["Estimate"])), ""),
                    row.names = NULL))
}
#
# extract a single fixed effect (e.g., an interaction) from a mixed-effects
# model (from `lmerTest::lmer`) and put the results together as a table
# -Note: with effect coding, the coefficient of a two-way interaction is a
#        quarter of the corresponding difference of differences, and the
#        coefficient of a three-way interaction is an eighth of the
#        corresponding difference. Thus, we also report this difference (i.e.,
#        `multiplier` times the coefficient) with its 95% confidence interval
#        (based on Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom), as well as the number of
#        observations and participants.
lmer_coef_tbl <- function(model, effect, multiplier = 4, coef_digits = 2, ...){
  # extract fixed effect
  fe <- coef(summary(model))[effect, ]
  # construct p-value
  pval <- ifelse(fe["Pr(>|t|)"] < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(fe["Pr(>|t|)"], 3))
  # implied difference and its 95% confidence interval
  diff <- unname(multiplier * fe["Estimate"])
  diff_se <- unname(multiplier * fe["Std. Error"])
  lower <- diff - qt(.975, unname(fe["df"])) * diff_se
  upper <- diff + qt(.975, unname(fe["df"])) * diff_se
  # construct return df
  fmt <- paste0("%.", coef_digits, "f")
  return(data.frame(estimate = sprintf(fmt, fe["Estimate"]),
                    std.error = sprintf("%.3f", fe["Std. Error"]),
                    difference = sprintf(fmt, diff),
                    ci = paste0("[", sprintf(fmt, lower), ", ", sprintf(fmt, upper), "]"),
                    test_statistic = paste0("t(", scales::comma(unname(fe["df"]), accuracy = .1), ") = ", sprintf('%.2f', fe["t value"])),
                    p = unname(pval),
                    observations = scales::comma(nobs(model)),
                    participants = scales::comma(unname(lme4::ngrps(model)["ID"])),
                    row.names = NULL))
}
#
# half a blank line between the paragraphs of the box labels in the procedure figure
half_gap <- function(label){
  paste0("<p>", gsub("<br><br>", "</p><p style='font-size:9pt'></p><p>", label, fixed = TRUE), "</p>")
}

# figure: Procedure of the experiment and preregistered analyses

# boxes of the procedure (first and second row), their labels, and their colors

            fill = "white", color = blue_dark, linewidth = .5) +
  geom_richtext(data = contrasts_boxes, aes(x = xmin + 1.3, y = ymax - 1.7, label = label),
                color = "gray15", fill = NA, label.color = NA, size = 3.6,
                family = "Roboto Condensed", lineheight = 1.15, hjust = 0, vjust = 1) +
  geom_segment(data = arrows_h, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), type = "closed"), color = "gray45") +
  geom_path(data = connector, aes(x = x, y = y),
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), type = "closed"), color = "gray45") +
  geom_segment(data = arrows_v, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), type = "closed"), color = "gray45") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(-11.5, 50), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10),
        plot.title = element_markdown(size = 18, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain",
                                      margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = 4, l = 0)),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, family = "Roboto Condensed",
                                     margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = 10, l = 0)),
        plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_markdown(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2, family = "Roboto Condensed", size = 10,
                                    margin = margin(t = 8, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0))) +
  labs(title = "<b>Procedure of the experiment and preregistered analyses</b>",
       subtitle = "Instruction condition between subjects, fluency and quality within subjects (Study 4)",
       caption = paste0("<i>Notes:</i><br>", "The four decks crossed visual fluency (high vs. low) with substantive quality (high vs. low).<br>",
                        "Each half (i.e., before and after the reminder) contained one high and one low fluency deck.<br>",
                        "Dark boxes: pitch decks and dependent variables; blue boxes: instruction manipulation; gray boxes: other parts of the survey;<br>",
                        "white boxes: preregistered analyses of the respective measures."))
```

# Data preparation

The data preparation steps included cleaning and preprocessing the survey data (from Qualtrics), which also contain the pitch deck tracking data (e.g., the viewing time per deck), and the demographic data (from Prolific). Next, the two data sources were merged, the preregistered exclusions were performed, and the final, processed datasets were saved. As preregistered, we excluded not only participants but also individual observations (i.e., a participant's responses to a single deck), namely when the deck was not loaded correctly, when it was viewed for less than 3 seconds or more than 30 minutes, or when it had no quality rating.

Note that in this report, we load the de-identified and anonymized datasets. Please consult the [online repository](https://researchbox.org/1836&PEER_REVIEW_passcode=NKVZFU) for the code that processed the raw data.

```{r}
#| label: load data
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: 'hide'

data_dir <- 'reproducibility_reports/data'

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Study 4: Design Disclosure and an Explanation of Processing Ease
# AsPredicted Preregistration #309446
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Getting and preparing the datasets
#
# Survey data (Qualtrics)
d_qua <- readr::read_csv(here(data_dir, 'Study_4_Qualtrics.csv'))

# how the conditions are encoded
#
# (1) Instruction condition (between participants): a balanced randomizer
#     assigned each participant to one of eight subgroups (`armchild` 1-8), which
#     belong to the three conditions in a 1:5:2 ratio (`arm`):
#       a1 = control (subgroup 1)
#       a2 = disclosure (subgroups 2-6)
#       a3 = disclosure plus explanation (subgroups 7-8)
# (2) Deck cells (within participants): every per-deck variable has a trailing
#     slot index (1-4). Slots 1 and 2 were shown before the midway reminder,
#     slots 3 and 4 after it. The rotation pattern (1-16) determines the cell of
#     each slot:
#       slot   patterns 1-8 (HQ first)   patterns 9-16 (LQ first)
#         1          HQ-HF                     LQ-HF
#         2          HQ-LF                     LQ-LF
#         3          LQ-HF                     HQ-HF
#         4          LQ-LF                     HQ-LF
#     (HQ/LQ = high/low quality, HF/LF = high/low fluency)
# (3) Display order: the two decks within each half, the four rating pages, and
#     the four ventures on the allocation page were shown in random order
#     (Qualtrics display order variables, *_DO)

# lookup tables
#
# instruction conditions
condition_labels <- c(a1 = "control", a2 = "disclosure", a3 = "disclosure_explanation")
# correct answers of the factual recovery questions: after each deck,
# participants answered one four-option question about the venture. The
# question was identical across the two design versions of a deck, but the
# correct answer depends on the content version (high vs. low quality)
recovery_correct_hq <- c(
  Servora   = "Its core patent has been granted, with further claims in prosecution.",
  Curato    = "Its founders built data infrastructure together at a leading AI-data company and left senior roles to work on Curato full-time.",
  Ironhall  = "Its module has passed independent industrial certification and already runs on live production lines.",
  Foliant   = "A bank customer has rolled Foliant out organization-wide after a successful pilot.",
  Pulsegrid = "Paying customers run it on production models, and it generates annual recurring revenue.",
  Paperloom = "An independent certification firm has completed an audit of its extraction accuracy and verified a benchmark lead.",
  Sentyl    = "It has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit, with the report available in its data room.",
  Axonmesh  = "Live fleets already coordinate robots in production at customer sites, billing recurring revenue."
)
recovery_correct_lq <- c(
  Servora   = "Its patent filing is a provisional application that is still pending.",
  Curato    = "Its founders are building Curato part-time alongside their current jobs, with the advisory board still forming.",
  Ironhall  = "Its industrial certification is still in testing, and its first module is installing on a pilot line this quarter.",
  Foliant   = "Its most advanced customer engagement is a pilot in two practice groups at a law firm.",
  Pulsegrid = "It is pre-revenue, with an open-beta cohort scheduled to start next month.",
  Paperloom = "An independent benchmark of its extraction accuracy is in progress but not yet finished.",
  Sentyl    = "Its SOC 2 Type II audit is scheduled but has not yet taken place.",
  Axonmesh  = "Its deployment to date is one pilot fleet running daily at a single design partner's warehouse."
)

# make variable names more coding friendly
d_qua_clean <- d_qua |>
  rename(IP_address = IPAddress,
         duration_study = `Duration (in seconds)`,
         attention_check_text = attention_check_99_TEXT,
         viewport_width = scr_w, viewport_height = scr_h,
         preload_first_half_raw = preload_1, preload_second_half_raw = preload_2,
         order_view_first_half_raw = FL_110_DO, order_view_second_half_raw = FL_114_DO,
         order_rating_raw = FL_123_DO, order_allocation_raw = advance_choice_DO) |>
  # conditions and randomizer records
  rename(condition_raw = arm, condition_group_raw = grp, condition_subgroup = armchild,
         randomizer_condition_subgroup_raw = FL_17_DO, randomizer_pattern_raw = FL_34_DO) |>
  # comprehension questions about the instruction message (up to three attempts)
  rename(comprehension_control_ventures_attempt1 = comp_ctrl1,
         comprehension_control_ventures_attempt2 = comp_ctrl1_r1,
         comprehension_control_ventures_attempt3 = comp_ctrl1_r2,
         comprehension_control_capital_attempt1 = comp_ctrl2,
         comprehension_control_capital_attempt2 = comp_ctrl2_r1,
         comprehension_control_capital_attempt3 = comp_ctrl2_r2,
         comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt1 = comp_act1,
         comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt2 = comp_act1_r1,
         comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt3 = comp_act1_r2,
         comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt1 = comp_act2,
         comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt2 = comp_act2_r1,
         comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt3 = comp_act2_r2,
         order_comprehension_control_ventures_attempt1_raw = comp_ctrl1_DO,
         order_comprehension_control_ventures_attempt2_raw = comp_ctrl1_r1_DO,
         order_comprehension_control_ventures_attempt3_raw = comp_ctrl1_r2_DO,
         order_comprehension_control_capital_attempt1_raw = comp_ctrl2_DO,
         order_comprehension_control_capital_attempt2_raw = comp_ctrl2_r1_DO,
         order_comprehension_control_capital_attempt3_raw = comp_ctrl2_r2_DO,
         order_comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt1_raw = comp_act1_DO,
         order_comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt2_raw = comp_act1_r1_DO,
         order_comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt3_raw = comp_act1_r2_DO,
         order_comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt1_raw = comp_act2_DO,
         order_comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt2_raw = comp_act2_r1_DO,
         order_comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt3_raw = comp_act2_r2_DO,
         # at least one answer wrong in attempt 1 / attempt 2 (1 = yes, 0 = no)
         comprehension_wrong_attempt1 = comp_r1, comprehension_wrong_attempt2 = comp_r2,
         comprehension_attempts = comp_attempts) |>
  # incentive comprehension question (up to two attempts)
  rename(incentive_comprehension_attempt1 = incentive_comprehension,
         incentive_comprehension_attempt2 = incentive_comprehension_r1,
         order_incentive_comprehension_attempt1_raw = incentive_comprehension_DO,
         order_incentive_comprehension_attempt2_raw = incentive_comprehension_r1_DO,
         # answer wrong in attempt 1 / attempt 2 (1 = yes, 0 = no)
         incentive_wrong_attempt1 = inc_r1, incentive_wrong_attempt2 = inc_r2,
         incentive_attempts = inc_attempts) |>
  # per-deck variables: from slot index to explicit slot suffix
  rename(pagetime_slot1 = `time_1_Page Submit`, pagetime_slot2 = `time_2_Page Submit`,
         pagetime_slot3 = `time_3_Page Submit`, pagetime_slot4 = `time_4_Page Submit`,
         firstclick_slot1 = `time_1_First Click`, firstclick_slot2 = `time_2_First Click`,
         firstclick_slot3 = `time_3_First Click`, firstclick_slot4 = `time_4_First Click`,
         lastclick_slot1 = `time_1_Last Click`, lastclick_slot2 = `time_2_Last Click`,
         lastclick_slot3 = `time_3_Last Click`, lastclick_slot4 = `time_4_Last Click`,
         clickcount_slot1 = `time_1_Click Count`, clickcount_slot2 = `time_2_Click Count`,
         clickcount_slot3 = `time_3_Click Count`, clickcount_slot4 = `time_4_Click Count`,
         viewtime_raw_slot1 = dwell_1, viewtime_raw_slot2 = dwell_2,
         viewtime_raw_slot3 = dwell_3, viewtime_raw_slot4 = dwell_4,
         coverage_raw_slot1 = cov_1, coverage_raw_slot2 = cov_2,
         coverage_raw_slot3 = cov_3, coverage_raw_slot4 = cov_4,
         imageload_raw_slot1 = imgok_1, imageload_raw_slot2 = imgok_2,
         imageload_raw_slot3 = imgok_3, imageload_raw_slot4 = imgok_4,
         venture_slot1 = d1_name, venture_slot2 = d2_name,
         venture_slot3 = d3_name, venture_slot4 = d4_name,
         sector_slot1 = d1_sub, sector_slot2 = d2_sub,
         sector_slot3 = d3_sub, sector_slot4 = d4_sub,
         deck_slot1 = d1_code, deck_slot2 = d2_code,
         deck_slot3 = d3_code, deck_slot4 = d4_code,
         allocation_slot1 = advance_choice_1, allocation_slot2 = advance_choice_2,
         allocation_slot3 = advance_choice_3, allocation_slot4 = advance_choice_4,
         ease_slot1 = fe_ease_1_1, ease_slot2 = fe_ease_2_1,
         ease_slot3 = fe_ease_3_1, ease_slot4 = fe_ease_4_1,
         rating_slot1 = end_quality_1, rating_slot2 = end_quality_2,
         rating_slot3 = end_quality_3, rating_slot4 = end_quality_4) |>
  # make all vars lower case (except for IDs)
  rename_at(vars(-ID, -PROLIFIC_PID, -IP_address), tolower)

# instruction condition and rotation sequence (high or low quality decks first)
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |>
  mutate(condition = unname(condition_labels[condition_raw]),
         sequence = ifelse(pattern <= 8, "hq_first", "lq_first"))

# comprehension of the instruction message
#   -Note: we record whether a participant also answered the third attempt
#          incorrectly (i.e., failed all three attempts). The correct answers are
#          "Four" and "100" (control) and "A design agency" and "Nothing" (both
#          disclosure conditions).
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |>
  mutate(comprehension_failed_all = comprehension_attempts == 3 &
           ifelse(condition == "control",
                  !(comprehension_control_ventures_attempt3 %in% "Four" &
                      comprehension_control_capital_attempt3 %in% 100),
                  !(comprehension_disclosure_designer_attempt3 %in% "A design agency" &
                      comprehension_disclosure_design_info_attempt3 %in% "Nothing")))

# decode the realized display order into positions (1-4), e.g., position_slot3 =
# 4 means that the deck in slot 3 was the last of the four decks shown
view_pos_1 <- display_position(d_qua_clean$order_view_first_half_raw, c("DeckSlot1", "DeckSlot2"))
view_pos_2 <- display_position(d_qua_clean$order_view_second_half_raw, c("DeckSlot3", "DeckSlot4"))
rating_pos <- display_position(d_qua_clean$order_rating_raw,
                               c("FeltEaseSlot1", "FeltEaseSlot2", "FeltEaseSlot3", "FeltEaseSlot4"))
alloc_pos <- display_position(d_qua_clean$order_allocation_raw,
                              c("${e://Field/d1_name} - ${e://Field/d1_sub}", "${e://Field/d2_name} - ${e://Field/d2_sub}",
                                "${e://Field/d3_name} - ${e://Field/d3_sub}", "${e://Field/d4_name} - ${e://Field/d4_sub}"))
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  # decks of the second half come after the two decks of the first half
  position_slot1 = view_pos_1$DeckSlot1, position_slot2 = view_pos_1$DeckSlot2,
  position_slot3 = view_pos_2$DeckSlot3 + 2, position_slot4 = view_pos_2$DeckSlot4 + 2,
  rating_position_slot1 = rating_pos$FeltEaseSlot1, rating_position_slot2 = rating_pos$FeltEaseSlot2,
  rating_position_slot3 = rating_pos$FeltEaseSlot3, rating_position_slot4 = rating_pos$FeltEaseSlot4,
  allocation_position_slot1 = alloc_pos[[1]], allocation_position_slot2 = alloc_pos[[2]],
  allocation_position_slot3 = alloc_pos[[3]], allocation_position_slot4 = alloc_pos[[4]]
)
rm(view_pos_1, view_pos_2, rating_pos, alloc_pos)

# decode the per-deck tracking data (recorded via JavaScript in Qualtrics):
# total viewing time (in seconds), number of slides viewed, and image loading
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  viewtime_slot1 = viewtime_sec(viewtime_raw_slot1), viewtime_slot2 = viewtime_sec(viewtime_raw_slot2),
  viewtime_slot3 = viewtime_sec(viewtime_raw_slot3), viewtime_slot4 = viewtime_sec(viewtime_raw_slot4),
  slides_seen_slot1 = slides_seen(coverage_raw_slot1), slides_seen_slot2 = slides_seen(coverage_raw_slot2),
  slides_seen_slot3 = slides_seen(coverage_raw_slot3), slides_seen_slot4 = slides_seen(coverage_raw_slot4),
  images_ok_slot1 = images_ok(imageload_raw_slot1), images_ok_slot2 = images_ok(imageload_raw_slot2),
  images_ok_slot3 = images_ok(imageload_raw_slot3), images_ok_slot4 = images_ok(imageload_raw_slot4)
)

# decode the factual recovery answers
#   -Note: for each slot, the export contains one question per venture (e.g.,
#          `rec1_servora`), but only the question of the venture shown in this
#          slot was displayed. we thus collapse the eight columns per slot
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  recovery_answer_slot1 = coalesce(rec1_servora, rec1_curato, rec1_ironhall, rec1_foliant,
                                   rec1_pulsegrid, rec1_paperloom, rec1_sentyl, rec1_axonmesh),
  recovery_answer_slot2 = coalesce(rec2_servora, rec2_curato, rec2_ironhall, rec2_foliant,
                                   rec2_pulsegrid, rec2_paperloom, rec2_sentyl, rec2_axonmesh),
  recovery_answer_slot3 = coalesce(rec3_servora, rec3_curato, rec3_ironhall, rec3_foliant,
                                   rec3_pulsegrid, rec3_paperloom, rec3_sentyl, rec3_axonmesh),
  recovery_answer_slot4 = coalesce(rec4_servora, rec4_curato, rec4_ironhall, rec4_foliant,
                                   rec4_pulsegrid, rec4_paperloom, rec4_sentyl, rec4_axonmesh)
)

# decode the slots into the experimental cells (see above)
#
# slot that holds the cell
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  slot_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", 1, 3),
  slot_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", 3, 1),
  slot_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", 2, 4),
  slot_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", 4, 2)
)
# venture information
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  venture_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", venture_slot1, venture_slot3),
  venture_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", venture_slot3, venture_slot1),
  venture_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", venture_slot2, venture_slot4),
  venture_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", venture_slot4, venture_slot2),

  sector_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", sector_slot1, sector_slot3),
  sector_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", sector_slot3, sector_slot1),
  sector_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", sector_slot2, sector_slot4),
  sector_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", sector_slot4, sector_slot2),

  deck_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", deck_slot1, deck_slot3),
  deck_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", deck_slot3, deck_slot1),
  deck_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", deck_slot2, deck_slot4),
  deck_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", deck_slot4, deck_slot2)
)
# dependent variables and further measures
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  rating_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_slot1, rating_slot3),
  rating_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_slot3, rating_slot1),
  rating_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_slot2, rating_slot4),
  rating_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_slot4, rating_slot2),

  ease_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", ease_slot1, ease_slot3),
  ease_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", ease_slot3, ease_slot1),
  ease_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", ease_slot2, ease_slot4),
  ease_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", ease_slot4, ease_slot2),

  allocation_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_slot1, allocation_slot3),
  allocation_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_slot3, allocation_slot1),
  allocation_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_slot2, allocation_slot4),
  allocation_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_slot4, allocation_slot2),

  recovery_answer_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", recovery_answer_slot1, recovery_answer_slot3),
  recovery_answer_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", recovery_answer_slot3, recovery_answer_slot1),
  recovery_answer_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", recovery_answer_slot2, recovery_answer_slot4),
  recovery_answer_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", recovery_answer_slot4, recovery_answer_slot2)
)
# display order
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  position_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", position_slot1, position_slot3),
  position_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", position_slot3, position_slot1),
  position_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", position_slot2, position_slot4),
  position_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", position_slot4, position_slot2),

  rating_position_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_position_slot1, rating_position_slot3),
  rating_position_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_position_slot3, rating_position_slot1),
  rating_position_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_position_slot2, rating_position_slot4),
  rating_position_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", rating_position_slot4, rating_position_slot2),

  allocation_position_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_position_slot1, allocation_position_slot3),
  allocation_position_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_position_slot3, allocation_position_slot1),
  allocation_position_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_position_slot2, allocation_position_slot4),
  allocation_position_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", allocation_position_slot4, allocation_position_slot2)
)
# per-deck data (page time in seconds, viewing time, slides viewed, image load)
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  pagetime_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", pagetime_slot1, pagetime_slot3),
  pagetime_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", pagetime_slot3, pagetime_slot1),
  pagetime_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", pagetime_slot2, pagetime_slot4),
  pagetime_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", pagetime_slot4, pagetime_slot2),

  viewtime_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", viewtime_slot1, viewtime_slot3),
  viewtime_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", viewtime_slot3, viewtime_slot1),
  viewtime_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", viewtime_slot2, viewtime_slot4),
  viewtime_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", viewtime_slot4, viewtime_slot2),

  slides_seen_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", slides_seen_slot1, slides_seen_slot3),
  slides_seen_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", slides_seen_slot3, slides_seen_slot1),
  slides_seen_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", slides_seen_slot2, slides_seen_slot4),
  slides_seen_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", slides_seen_slot4, slides_seen_slot2),

  images_ok_hq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", images_ok_slot1, images_ok_slot3),
  images_ok_lq_hf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", images_ok_slot3, images_ok_slot1),
  images_ok_hq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", images_ok_slot2, images_ok_slot4),
  images_ok_lq_lf = ifelse(sequence == "hq_first", images_ok_slot4, images_ok_slot2)
)
# score the factual recovery answers: an answer is correct (= 1) if it matches
# the correct answer for the content version of the venture shown in the cell
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> mutate(
  recovery_correct_hq_hf = as.numeric(recovery_answer_hq_hf == recovery_correct_hq[venture_hq_hf]),
  recovery_correct_hq_lf = as.numeric(recovery_answer_hq_lf == recovery_correct_hq[venture_hq_lf]),
  recovery_correct_lq_hf = as.numeric(recovery_answer_lq_hf == recovery_correct_lq[venture_lq_hf]),
  recovery_correct_lq_lf = as.numeric(recovery_answer_lq_lf == recovery_correct_lq[venture_lq_lf])
)

# remove the variables that are replaced by the variables created above
#   -Note: this has to happen before the exclusions, since, e.g., the recovery
#          questions of the ventures not shown are always missing
d_qua_clean <- d_qua_clean |> select(-c(
  # condition assignment (replaced by `condition`, `condition_subgroup`, `pattern`)
  condition_raw, condition_group_raw,
  randomizer_condition_subgroup_raw, randomizer_pattern_raw,
  # comprehension questions about the instruction message (replaced by
  # `comprehension_attempts` and `comprehension_failed_all`)
  starts_with("comprehension_control_"), starts_with("comprehension_disclosure_"),
  starts_with("order_comprehension_"),
  comprehension_wrong_attempt1, comprehension_wrong_attempt2,
  # incentive comprehension question (replaced by `incentive_attempts`)
  incentive_comprehension_attempt1, incentive_comprehension_attempt2,
  order_incentive_comprehension_attempt1_raw, order_incentive_comprehension_attempt2_raw,
  incentive_wrong_attempt1, incentive_wrong_attempt2,
  # factual recovery questions per slot and venture and their answer option
  # orders (replaced by `recovery_answer_slot1` to `recovery_answer_slot4`)
  matches("^rec[1-4]_"),
  # display order records (replaced by the position variables)
  order_view_first_half_raw, order_view_second_half_raw,
  order_rating_raw, order_allocation_raw,
  # per-slot variables (replaced by the cell versions)
  starts_with(c("venture_slot", "sector_slot", "deck_slot",
                "rating_slot", "ease_slot", "allocation_slot",
                "position_slot", "rating_position_slot", "allocation_position_slot",
                "pagetime_slot", "viewtime_raw_slot", "viewtime_slot",
                "coverage_raw_slot", "slides_seen_slot",
                "imageload_raw_slot", "images_ok_slot")),
  recovery_answer_slot1, recovery_answer_slot2, recovery_answer_slot3, recovery_answer_slot4
))

# Demographic data (Prolific)
d_pro <- readr::read_csv(here(data_dir, 'Study_4_Prolific.csv'))
# make variable names more coding friendly
d_pro_clean <- d_pro |>
  rename(investment_types = `Types of investment`, ethnicity = `Ethnicity simplified`,
         country = `Country of residence`, employment = `Employment status`) |>
  rename_at(vars(-ID), tolower)
# remove age and sex from the data, since we explicitly asked this information
# in Qualtrics
d_pro_clean <- d_pro_clean |>
  select(-age, -sex)

# Merging the data
#
# merge Qualtrics and Prolific data
d_all <- full_join(d_qua_clean, d_pro_clean, by = "ID")
# to make typing easier, let's call our data d for now
d <- d_all
rm(d_all, d_pro, d_pro_clean, d_qua, d_qua_clean, condition_labels,
   recovery_correct_hq, recovery_correct_lq)

# Exclusions (participant level)
#
# participants did not give consent (or did not answer but closed survey or
# returned study submission)
d <- d |> filter(!(consent != "yes"))
# incomplete responses
#   -Note: the exceptions are the text field of the "other" option and
#          demographic information from Prolific (may be expired)
d <- d |> tidyr::drop_na(!c(attention_check_text, investment_types, ethnicity,
                            country, nationality, employment))
# Prolific ID is missing
d <- d |> filter(!(is.na(ID)))
# reported Prolific ID (ID) is different from actual Prolific ID
d <- d |> filter(!(ID != PROLIFIC_PID))
# Prolific submission returned or timed out
d <- d |> filter(!(status %in% c("RETURNED", "TIMED-OUT")))
# duplicate Prolific IDs (first complete response is kept)
d <- d |> arrange(startdate) |> group_by(ID) |> slice(1) |> ungroup()
# duplicate IP Address (first complete response is kept)
d <- d |> arrange(startdate) |> group_by(IP_address) |> slice(1) |> ungroup()
# duration to complete survey more than 60 minutes
#   -Note: `duration_study` was measured in seconds
#          thus 60 minutes = 3600 seconds
d <- d |> filter(!(duration_study > 3600))
# participants failed attention check
#
# check which answers were given in text field
# unique(d$attention_check_text[d$attention_check == "Other"])
#
# versions of correct answers
str_attention_correct <- c(
  "I have read this text carefully",
  "i have read this text carefully",
  "I HAVE READ THIS TEXT CAREFULLY",
  "I have read this carefully",
  "I have read this text carefully.",
  "I have read this text caefully",
  "I  have read this text carefully",
  "I have read ths text carefully",
  "I have read the text carefully",
  "I have read this text carefuly",
  "\"I have read this text carefully\"",
  "I have read this text carrefully",
  "I have read this text carefully\n",
  "I have read this text careffully",
  "\u201cI have read this text carefully\u201d",
  "I have read this text carefully\u201d into the text field",
  "I have ready this text carefully",
  "I have raed this text carefully",
  "\"I have read this text carefully\u201d",
  "''I have read this text carefully''",
  "I have read the text carefully."
)
# exclude participants with an answer not listed above
d <- d |> filter(!(attention_check != "Other" |
                 attention_check_text %notin% str_attention_correct))

# Exclusions (observation level)
#
# --Note: An observation is one participant's responses to one deck. Thus, we
#         do not remove whole participants but set the deck-level dependent
#         variables (quality rating, capital allocation, factual recovery) of an
#         invalid deck to NA. A deck is invalid if (1) the slide deck was not
#         correctly loaded, (2) the slide deck was viewed for less than 3
#         seconds or more than 30 minutes, or (3) there is no quality rating.
#         The manipulation checks are not affected by these exclusions; we thus
#         keep a copy of the quality ratings of all decks (`rating_all_*`), and
#         felt ease is not set to NA.
#
# (1) slide deck not correctly loaded
#     -> see `images_ok_*` from above
#
# (2) slide deck viewed for less than 3 seconds or more than 30 minutes
d <- d |> mutate(
  viewtime_off_hq_hf = is.na(viewtime_hq_hf) | viewtime_hq_hf < 3 | viewtime_hq_hf > 1800,
  viewtime_off_lq_hf = is.na(viewtime_lq_hf) | viewtime_lq_hf < 3 | viewtime_lq_hf > 1800,
  viewtime_off_hq_lf = is.na(viewtime_hq_lf) | viewtime_hq_lf < 3 | viewtime_hq_lf > 1800,
  viewtime_off_lq_lf = is.na(viewtime_lq_lf) | viewtime_lq_lf < 3 | viewtime_lq_lf > 1800
)
# (3) no quality rating
#   -Note: the quality rating was a forced-response item, so this criterion
#          should never apply after the exclusion of incomplete responses
d <- d |> mutate(
  rating_missing_hq_hf = is.na(rating_hq_hf),
  rating_missing_lq_hf = is.na(rating_lq_hf),
  rating_missing_hq_lf = is.na(rating_hq_lf),
  rating_missing_lq_lf = is.na(rating_lq_lf)
)
# combine the three criteria into one "invalid" flag per deck
d <- d |> mutate(
  invalid_hq_hf = !images_ok_hq_hf | viewtime_off_hq_hf | rating_missing_hq_hf,
  invalid_lq_hf = !images_ok_lq_hf | viewtime_off_lq_hf | rating_missing_lq_hf,
  invalid_hq_lf = !images_ok_hq_lf | viewtime_off_hq_lf | rating_missing_hq_lf,
  invalid_lq_lf = !images_ok_lq_lf | viewtime_off_lq_lf | rating_missing_lq_lf
)
# keep a copy of the ratings of all decks (for the manipulation check)
d <- d |> mutate(
  rating_all_hq_hf = rating_hq_hf,
  rating_all_lq_hf = rating_lq_hf,
  rating_all_hq_lf = rating_hq_lf,
  rating_all_lq_lf = rating_lq_lf
)
# set the deck-level dependent variables of every invalid deck to NA
d <- d |> mutate(
  rating_hq_hf = ifelse(invalid_hq_hf, NA, rating_hq_hf),
  rating_lq_hf = ifelse(invalid_lq_hf, NA, rating_lq_hf),
  rating_hq_lf = ifelse(invalid_hq_lf, NA, rating_hq_lf),
  rating_lq_lf = ifelse(invalid_lq_lf, NA, rating_lq_lf),
  allocation_hq_hf = ifelse(invalid_hq_hf, NA, allocation_hq_hf),
  allocation_lq_hf = ifelse(invalid_lq_hf, NA, allocation_lq_hf),
  allocation_hq_lf = ifelse(invalid_hq_lf, NA, allocation_hq_lf),
  allocation_lq_lf = ifelse(invalid_lq_lf, NA, allocation_lq_lf),
  recovery_correct_hq_hf = ifelse(invalid_hq_hf, NA, recovery_correct_hq_hf),
  recovery_correct_lq_hf = ifelse(invalid_lq_hf, NA, recovery_correct_lq_hf),
  recovery_correct_hq_lf = ifelse(invalid_hq_lf, NA, recovery_correct_hq_lf),
  recovery_correct_lq_lf = ifelse(invalid_lq_lf, NA, recovery_correct_lq_lf)
)

# Preregistered contrasts
#
# fluency contrast = mean(high-fluency decks) - mean(low-fluency decks)
# quality contrast = mean(high-quality decks) - mean(low-quality decks)
#   -Note: the contrasts are computed for the quality ratings (primary DV, in
#          rating points) and for the capital allocation (in units out of 100).
#          They are NA if any of the four decks is invalid.
d <- d |> mutate(
  fluency_contrast_rating = rowMeans(pick(rating_hq_hf, rating_lq_hf)) -
                            rowMeans(pick(rating_hq_lf, rating_lq_lf)),
  quality_contrast_rating = rowMeans(pick(rating_hq_hf, rating_hq_lf)) -
                            rowMeans(pick(rating_lq_hf, rating_lq_lf)),
  fluency_contrast_allocation = rowMeans(pick(allocation_hq_hf, allocation_lq_hf)) -
                                rowMeans(pick(allocation_hq_lf, allocation_lq_lf)),
  quality_contrast_allocation = rowMeans(pick(allocation_hq_hf, allocation_hq_lf)) -
                                rowMeans(pick(allocation_lq_hf, allocation_lq_lf))
)

# Covariates
#
# group "Non-binary" and "Prefer not to say" gender categories into one
d$gender <- forcats::fct_collapse(d$gender, Female = "Female", Male = "Male", other_level = "Other")

# keep only the variables that are needed for the analyses
d <- d |>
  select(
    # identifier
    ID,
    # experimental design: condition, rotation pattern and venture assignment
    condition, condition_subgroup, pattern, sequence,
    slot_hq_hf, slot_lq_hf, slot_hq_lf, slot_lq_lf,
    venture_hq_hf, venture_lq_hf, venture_hq_lf, venture_lq_lf,
    deck_hq_hf, deck_lq_hf, deck_hq_lf, deck_lq_lf,
    sector_hq_hf, sector_lq_hf, sector_hq_lf, sector_lq_lf,
    # experimental design: realized display order
    position_hq_hf, position_lq_hf, position_hq_lf, position_lq_lf,
    rating_position_hq_hf, rating_position_lq_hf, rating_position_hq_lf, rating_position_lq_lf,
    allocation_position_hq_hf, allocation_position_lq_hf,
    allocation_position_hq_lf, allocation_position_lq_lf,
    # primary DV (quality ratings, invalid decks set to NA)
    rating_hq_hf, rating_lq_hf, rating_hq_lf, rating_lq_lf,
    # further DVs (invalid decks set to NA)
    allocation_hq_hf, allocation_lq_hf, allocation_hq_lf, allocation_lq_lf,
    recovery_correct_hq_hf, recovery_correct_lq_hf, recovery_correct_hq_lf, recovery_correct_lq_lf,
    # preregistered contrasts
    fluency_contrast_rating, quality_contrast_rating,
    fluency_contrast_allocation, quality_contrast_allocation,
    # manipulation checks (all decks)
    ease_hq_hf, ease_lq_hf, ease_hq_lf, ease_lq_lf,
    rating_all_hq_hf, rating_all_lq_hf, rating_all_hq_lf, rating_all_lq_lf,
    # beliefs about the informativeness of the design
    belief_quality, belief_founders,
    # per-deck data
    recovery_answer_hq_hf, recovery_answer_lq_hf, recovery_answer_hq_lf, recovery_answer_lq_lf,
    viewtime_hq_hf, viewtime_lq_hf, viewtime_hq_lf, viewtime_lq_lf,
    pagetime_hq_hf, pagetime_lq_hf, pagetime_hq_lf, pagetime_lq_lf,
    slides_seen_hq_hf, slides_seen_lq_hf, slides_seen_hq_lf, slides_seen_lq_lf,
    images_ok_hq_hf, images_ok_lq_hf, images_ok_hq_lf, images_ok_lq_lf,
    invalid_hq_hf, invalid_lq_hf, invalid_hq_lf, invalid_lq_lf,
    # comprehension of the instructions
    comprehension_attempts, comprehension_failed_all, incentive_attempts,
    # covariates and individual differences
    age, gender, invest_experience,
    # prolific demographics
    investment_types, ethnicity, country, nationality, employment,
    # checks and probes
    suspicion_probe, funnel_about,
    # study meta-information
    duration_study, viewport_width, viewport_height
  )

# Long format
#
# the mixed-effects models need one row per participant x deck (i.e., 4 rows
# per participant). we build the long format by hand: for each of the 4 cells,
# we create a small data frame with the same variables, and we stack them
# afterwards
#   -Note: `half` indicates whether the deck was shown before (first) or after
#          (second) the midway reminder
d_hq_hf <- d |>
  mutate(ID, condition, pattern, sequence,
        cell = "hq_hf",
        quality = "high",  fluency = "high",
        venture = venture_hq_hf, deck = deck_hq_hf, slot = slot_hq_hf,
        position = position_hq_hf, half = ifelse(position_hq_hf <= 2, "first", "second"),
        rating_position = rating_position_hq_hf, allocation_position = allocation_position_hq_hf,
        rating = rating_hq_hf, allocation = allocation_hq_hf,
        recovery_correct = recovery_correct_hq_hf,
        ease = ease_hq_hf, rating_all = rating_all_hq_hf,
        viewtime = viewtime_hq_hf, pagetime = pagetime_hq_hf, slides_seen = slides_seen_hq_hf,
        invalid = invalid_hq_hf,
        .keep = "none") # .keep = "none" keeps only the variables listed above

d_lq_hf <- d |>
  mutate(ID, condition, pattern, sequence,
        cell = "lq_hf",
        quality = "low",   fluency = "high",
        venture = venture_lq_hf, deck = deck_lq_hf, slot = slot_lq_hf,
        position = position_lq_hf, half = ifelse(position_lq_hf <= 2, "first", "second"),
        rating_position = rating_position_lq_hf, allocation_position = allocation_position_lq_hf,
        rating = rating_lq_hf, allocation = allocation_lq_hf,
        recovery_correct = recovery_correct_lq_hf,
        ease = ease_lq_hf, rating_all = rating_all_lq_hf,
        viewtime = viewtime_lq_hf, pagetime = pagetime_lq_hf, slides_seen = slides_seen_lq_hf,
        invalid = invalid_lq_hf,
        .keep = "none")

d_hq_lf <- d |>
  mutate(ID, condition, pattern, sequence,
        cell = "hq_lf",
        quality = "high",  fluency = "low",
        venture = venture_hq_lf, deck = deck_hq_lf, slot = slot_hq_lf,
        position = position_hq_lf, half = ifelse(position_hq_lf <= 2, "first", "second"),
        rating_position = rating_position_hq_lf, allocation_position = allocation_position_hq_lf,
        rating = rating_hq_lf, allocation = allocation_hq_lf,
        recovery_correct = recovery_correct_hq_lf,
        ease = ease_hq_lf, rating_all = rating_all_hq_lf,
        viewtime = viewtime_hq_lf, pagetime = pagetime_hq_lf, slides_seen = slides_seen_hq_lf,
        invalid = invalid_hq_lf,
        .keep = "none")

d_lq_lf <- d |>
  mutate(ID, condition, pattern, sequence,
        cell = "lq_lf",
        quality = "low",   fluency = "low",
        venture = venture_lq_lf, deck = deck_lq_lf, slot = slot_lq_lf,
        position = position_lq_lf, half = ifelse(position_lq_lf <= 2, "first", "second"),
        rating_position = rating_position_lq_lf, allocation_position = allocation_position_lq_lf,
        rating = rating_lq_lf, allocation = allocation_lq_lf,
        recovery_correct = recovery_correct_lq_lf,
        ease = ease_lq_lf, rating_all = rating_all_lq_lf,
        viewtime = viewtime_lq_lf, pagetime = pagetime_lq_lf, slides_seen = slides_seen_lq_lf,
        invalid = invalid_lq_lf,
        .keep = "none")

# put everything together
d_long <- bind_rows(d_hq_hf, d_lq_hf, d_hq_lf, d_lq_lf)
rm(d_hq_hf, d_lq_hf, d_hq_lf, d_lq_lf)

# add covariates and demographics
d_long <- d_long |>
  left_join(d |> select(ID, belief_quality, belief_founders,
                        comprehension_attempts, comprehension_failed_all,
                        suspicion_probe, age, gender, invest_experience,
                        investment_types, ethnicity, country, nationality,
                        employment),
            by = "ID")
```



# Descriptives

@tbl-obs gives a demographic overview of the dataset per instruction condition.
Moreover, @tbl-randomization-check shows which startups appeared in which version in each of the sixteen rotation patterns and whether the two high quality or the two low quality decks were shown before the reminder. It also shows the final N per rotation pattern and condition after the preregistered exclusions. Across the conditions, these numbers reflect the 1:5:2 assignment ratio.
@tbl-descriptives-1 and @tbl-descriptives-allocation-1 show a descriptive breakdown of the perceived venture quality ratings (i.e., the main dependent variable) and of the investment allocation by instruction condition, visual fluency, and substantive quality, and @tbl-descriptives-2 and @tbl-descriptives-allocation-2 show the participant-level contrasts that we used in the analyses (cf. @sec-main).

Note that the observation-level exclusions affected `r sum(d_long$invalid)` of the `r scales::comma(nrow(d_long))` decks. Thus, the analyzable sample for the confirmatory tests, that is, all participants with four valid decks, comprises `r sum(!is.na(d$fluency_contrast_rating))` participants (control: `r sum(!is.na(d$fluency_contrast_rating[d$condition == "control"]))`; disclosure: `r sum(!is.na(d$fluency_contrast_rating[d$condition == "disclosure"]))`; disclosure plus explanation: `r sum(!is.na(d$fluency_contrast_rating[d$condition == "disclosure_explanation"]))`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-obs
#| tbl-cap: 'Sample overview per instruction condition'

# convert condition into factor (for the tables)
d$Condition <- factor(d$condition, levels = c("control", "disclosure", "disclosure_explanation"),
                      labels = c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure + explanation"))

# create demographics table
d |>
  group_by(Condition) |>
  summarize(N = n(),
            Age = round(mean(age, na.rm = T), 2),
            `% Female`= round(prop.table(table(gender))["Female"]*100, 1),
    `Investment Experience` = paste0(weights::rd(mean(invest_experience, na.rm = T), 2), " (±", weights::rd(sd(invest_experience, na.rm = T), 2), ")"),
            `% White` = round(prop.table(table(ethnicity))["White"]*100, 1),
            `% US` = round(prop.table(table(country))["United States"]*100, 1),
            `% Full-Time Empl.` = round(prop.table(table(employment))["Full-Time"]*100, 1)
            ) |> kbl() |> kable_styling()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-randomization-check
#| tbl-cap: 'Rotation patterns and randomization check'

d |> group_by(Pattern = pattern) |>
  summarize(
    # decks shown before the midway reminder
    first_half = ifelse(unique(sequence) == "hq_first", "High quality", "Low quality"),
    # startups per combination of fluency and quality
    hf_hq = unique(venture_hq_hf), hf_lq = unique(venture_lq_hf),
    lf_hq = unique(venture_hq_lf), lf_lq = unique(venture_lq_lf),
    # final N per condition
    n_control = sum(condition == "control"),
    n_disclosure = sum(condition == "disclosure"),
    n_explanation = sum(condition == "disclosure_explanation")
  ) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Pattern", "Decks Before Reminder", rep(c("High Quality", "Low Quality"), 2),
                    "Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure + Explanation"),
      align = "ccccccccc") |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(2, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;") |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "High Fluency" = 2, "Low Fluency" = 2, " " = 3)) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Startup per Deck Version" = 4, "Final N per Condition" = 3))
```

::: {#tbl-descriptives layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-descriptives-1}

```{r}
# analyzable sample: participants with four valid decks
d_valid <- d |> filter(!is.na(fluency_contrast_rating))
d_long_valid <- d_long |> filter(ID %in% d_valid$ID)

# ratings per condition and experimental cell
# --Note: `group_by(fluency, quality)` orders the cells as HF-HQ, HF-LQ, LF-HQ, LF-LQ
d_long_valid |> filter(condition == "control") |> group_by(fluency, quality) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(rating), SD = sd(rating)) |> ungroup() -> temp_ctrl
d_long_valid |> filter(condition == "disclosure") |> group_by(fluency, quality) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(rating), SD = sd(rating)) |> ungroup() -> temp_disc
d_long_valid |> filter(condition == "disclosure_explanation") |> group_by(fluency, quality) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(rating), SD = sd(rating)) |> ungroup() -> temp_expl
temp_cells <- data.frame(
  fluency = c("High", "High", "Low", "Low"),
  quality = c("High", "Low", "High", "Low"),
  N_ctrl = temp_ctrl$N, Mean_ctrl = temp_ctrl$Mean, SD_ctrl = temp_ctrl$SD,
  N_disc = temp_disc$N, Mean_disc = temp_disc$Mean, SD_disc = temp_disc$SD,
  N_expl = temp_expl$N, Mean_expl = temp_expl$Mean, SD_expl = temp_expl$SD)

temp_cells |>
  kbl(digits = 2, col.names = c("Fluency", "Quality", rep(c("N", "Mean", "SD"), 3)), align = "llccccccccc") |>
  kable_styling() |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Control" = 3, "Disclosure" = 3, "Disclosure + Explanation" = 3)) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Perceived Venture Quality Rating per Deck (1–7)" = 9))
```

```{r}
# participant-level contrasts (in rating points) per condition
d_valid |> group_by(condition) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(fluency_contrast_rating), SD = sd(fluency_contrast_rating)) -> temp_fluency
d_valid |> group_by(condition) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(quality_contrast_rating), SD = sd(quality_contrast_rating)) -> temp_quality
temp_contrasts <- data.frame(
  row = c("Fluency contrast", "Quality contrast"),
  N_ctrl = c(temp_fluency$N[1], temp_quality$N[1]),

temp_contrasts |>

  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Control" = 3, "Disclosure" = 3, "Disclosure + Explanation" = 3)) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Participant-Level Contrast (High Minus Low Level, in Rating Points)" = 9)) |>
  column_spec(1, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

```{r}
# allocation per condition and experimental cell
d_long_valid |> filter(condition == "control") |> group_by(fluency, quality) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(allocation), SD = sd(allocation)) |> ungroup() -> temp_ctrl
d_long_valid |> filter(condition == "disclosure") |> group_by(fluency, quality) |>

d_long_valid |> filter(condition == "disclosure_explanation") |> group_by(fluency, quality) |>
  summarize(N = n(), Mean = mean(allocation), SD = sd(allocation)) |> ungroup() -> temp_expl
temp_cells <- data.frame(
  fluency = c("High", "High", "Low", "Low"),
  quality = c("High", "Low", "High", "Low"),
  N_ctrl = temp_ctrl$N, Mean_ctrl = temp_ctrl$Mean, SD_ctrl = temp_ctrl$SD,
  N_disc = temp_disc$N, Mean_disc = temp_disc$Mean, SD_disc = temp_disc$SD,
  N_expl = temp_expl$N, Mean_expl = temp_expl$Mean, SD_expl = temp_expl$SD)

temp_cells |>
  kbl(digits = 2, col.names = c("Fluency", "Quality", rep(c("N", "Mean", "SD"), 3)), align = "llccccccccc") |>
  kable_styling() |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Control" = 3, "Disclosure" = 3, "Disclosure + Explanation" = 3)) |>
```
