# Results {#sec-results}

In this section, we first report the preregistered confirmatory tests and the preregistered decision rule for the disclosure condition. @sec-further, @sec-mc, @sec-sensitivity, and @sec-exploratory then show the results of the further preregistered measures, the manipulation checks, the sensitivity analyses, and the exploratory analyses, respectively.


## Main analyses {#sec-main}

As preregistered, we computed for each participant a fluency contrast on the perceived venture quality ratings (in rating points):

$$
\text{FC}_{i} = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{d \in \text{HF}_{i}} r_{id} - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{d \in \text{LF}_{i}} r_{id},
$$

where $r_{id}$ is participant $i$'s perceived venture quality rating (1–7) of deck $d$, and $\text{HF}_{i}$ and $\text{LF}_{i}$ are the two high and the two low fluency decks that the participant saw. Since each of these two sets contains one high and one low quality deck, substantive quality is balanced out of the fluency contrast by construction. For completeness, we also computed the analogous quality contrast (the two high minus the two low quality decks) and the same contrasts on the allocated units. For example, a fluency contrast of 0.5 means that the two high fluency decks were rated, on average, half a rating point higher than the two low fluency decks. All confirmatory tests use the analyzable sample (i.e., participants with four valid decks).

The preregistered predictions were that the fluency contrast is positive in the control condition, that it remains positive in the disclosure condition, and that it is smaller in the disclosure plus explanation condition than in the disclosure condition (hypotheses H1, H2, and H3 in the preregistration, Hypotheses 3, 4, and 5 in the paper). @tbl-results-contrasts shows the results of the one-sample t-tests of the fluency contrast against zero. For the control condition (@tbl-results-contrasts-1), we preregistered a one-sided test (fluency contrast > 0). For the disclosure condition (@tbl-results-contrasts-2), we preregistered a two-sided test together with the 95% confidence interval and the Bayes factor (BF<sub>10</sub>; default Cauchy prior with r = 0.707, point null at zero). All confidence intervals are two-sided, also for the one-sided test.

::: {#tbl-results-contrasts layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-results-contrasts-1}

```{r}
# convert condition into factor
d$condition <- factor(d$condition, levels = c("control", "disclosure", "disclosure_explanation"))
d_long$condition <- factor(d_long$condition, levels = c("control", "disclosure", "disclosure_explanation"))
d_valid$condition <- factor(d_valid$condition, levels = c("control", "disclosure", "disclosure_explanation"))

# fluency contrast (quality ratings) per condition
contrast_control <- d_valid$fluency_contrast_rating[d_valid$condition == "control"]
contrast_disclosure <- d_valid$fluency_contrast_rating[d_valid$condition == "disclosure"]
contrast_explanation <- d_valid$fluency_contrast_rating[d_valid$condition == "disclosure_explanation"]

# one-sided test (control condition)
contrast_tbl(contrast_control, alternative = "greater") |>
  mutate(Condition = "Control") |>
  select(Condition, N, Mean, SD, CI, test_statistic, p, d) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "95% CI", "t-test", "p (one-sided)", "Cohen's d<sub>z</sub>"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(c(5, 6), extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

Control condition (one-sided test)
:::

::: {#tbl-results-contrasts-2}

```{r}
# two-sided test and Bayes factor (disclosure condition)
bf10_h2 <- BayesFactor::extractBF(
  BayesFactor::ttestBF(x = contrast_disclosure, mu = 0, rscale = 0.707))$bf

contrast_tbl(contrast_disclosure, alternative = "two.sided") |>
  mutate(Condition = "Disclosure", BF = bf_fmt(bf10_h2)) |>
  select(Condition, N, Mean, SD, CI, test_statistic, p, d, BF) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "95% CI", "t-test", "p (two-sided)", "Cohen's d<sub>z</sub>", "BF<sub>10</sub>"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(c(5, 6), extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")

# 90% confidence interval and equivalence test (disclosure condition; for the text below)
ci90_h2 <- t.test(contrast_disclosure, conf.level = .90)$conf.int
equivalence_h2 <- t.test(contrast_disclosure, mu = -eq_bound, alternative = "greater")$p.value < .05 &
  t.test(contrast_disclosure, mu = eq_bound, alternative = "less")$p.value < .05
# secondary test: Welch ANOVA across the three conditions (for the text below)
welch_anova <- oneway.test(fluency_contrast_rating ~ condition, data = d_valid, var.equal = FALSE)
```

::: {.table-note style="font-size: 80%; text-align: left;"}
*Notes:* `r bf_note(bf10_h2, "a fluency contrast different from zero")`
:::

Disclosure condition (two-sided test)
:::

Preregistered one-sample t-tests of the fluency contrast (in rating points)
:::

In addition, we preregistered an equivalence test for the disclosure condition, that is, two one-sided tests at α = .05 against the bounds of -0.225 and +0.225 rating points. Equivalence is concluded if both one-sided tests are significant, which is the same as the 90% confidence interval lying inside the bounds. @tbl-results-h2-1 shows the results of this equivalence test. The 90% confidence interval of the fluency contrast in the disclosure condition is [`r weights::rd(ci90_h2[1], 2)`, `r weights::rd(ci90_h2[2], 2)`]. Hence, equivalence is `r ifelse(equivalence_h2, "established", "not established")`. Moreover, @tbl-results-h2-2 shows the preregistered comparisons between the conditions (Welch t-tests on the fluency contrast): the comparison of the control and the disclosure condition (two-sided), which is part of the decision rule below, and the comparison of the two disclosure conditions, that is, whether the added explanation reduces the fluency contrast compared to disclosure alone (one-sided). As a secondary test, a Welch ANOVA across all three conditions yielded F(`r welch_anova$parameter[1]`, `r weights::rd(welch_anova$parameter[2], 1)`) = `r sprintf('%.2f', welch_anova$statistic)`, p = `r weights::rd(welch_anova$p.value, 3)`.

::: {#tbl-results-h2 layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-results-h2-1}

```{r}
# equivalence test (TOST)
tost_tbl(contrast_disclosure, bound = eq_bound) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("One-Sided Test", "t-test", "p (one-sided)"), escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling()
```

Equivalence test (TOST) of the fluency contrast in the disclosure condition (bounds of ±0.225 rating points)
:::

::: {#tbl-results-h2-2}

```{r}
# comparisons between conditions
# --Note: control vs. disclosure is tested two-sided, disclosure vs. disclosure
#         plus explanation one-sided (first > second)
temp <- bind_rows(
  welch_tbl(contrast_control, contrast_disclosure, alternative = "two.sided"),
  welch_tbl(contrast_disclosure, contrast_explanation, alternative = "greater")
)
temp$p_two_sided <- c(temp$p[1], NA)
temp$p_one_sided <- c(NA, temp$p[2])
temp |>
  mutate(Comparison = c("Control vs. disclosure", "Disclosure vs. disclosure + explanation")) |>
  select(Comparison, N_1, N_2, Mean_1, Mean_2, test_statistic, p_two_sided, p_one_sided, d) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Comparison", "N (First)", "N (Second)", "Mean (First)", "Mean (Second)", "t-test",
                    "p (two-sided)", "p (one-sided, first > second)", "Cohen's d"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(6, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")

# preregistered decision rule for the disclosure condition (see below)
decision_h2 <- h2_decision(contrast_disclosure, contrast_control)
```

Comparisons of the fluency contrast between conditions (Welch t-tests)
:::

Equivalence test and comparisons between conditions
:::

The preregistered decision rule for the disclosure condition was as follows:

1. The fluency contrast is significantly negative with the estimate at or beyond the bound (-0.225): overcorrection.
2. The fluency contrast is significantly positive with the estimate at least 0.225: persistence supported.
3. Equivalence passes and the comparison of the control and the disclosure condition is significant with the fluency contrast being higher in the control condition: switched off (any significant effect remaining inside the bound is reported as such, in either direction).
4. The fluency contrast is significantly positive but below 0.225 without passing equivalence: reduced but present.
5. Otherwise: indeterminate.

Applying this decision rule to the results above yields case `r h2_step(decision_h2)` (`r h2_outcome(decision_h2)`). @fig-decision shows which case other estimates would have yielded.


## Further preregistered measures {#sec-further}

As preregistered, the two further measures (factual recovery and investment allocation) were estimated in the disclosure condition. The same quantities in the other conditions are exploratory (unless noted otherwise). In addition, we preregistered a check of the participants' beliefs about the informativeness of the design.

### Factual recovery

After each deck, participants answered one four-option question about a substantive fact of the startup. We estimated a mixed logistic regression that predicts a correct answer by visual fluency and substantive quality, with random intercepts for participants and startups. As preregistered, only the fluency effect is interpreted, and the preregistered test concerns the disclosure condition. The models for the other two conditions are exploratory. Both factors were effect-coded (i.e., `low` as `-1` and `high` as `+1`). With this coding, the difference in log-odds between the high and the low condition is two times the coefficient, and the odds ratio (high vs. low) is thus exp(2 × coefficient). We used the bobyqa optimizer, since the model for the disclosure condition did not converge with the default optimizer. The model for the control condition has a singular fit (i.e., the estimated startup variance is zero). The answers to invalid decks are not included, so that the models are based on all participants with at least one valid deck. @tbl-results-recovery shows the observed share of correct answers per condition and fluency level, together with the fluency effect in the mixed logistic regressions.

::: {#tbl-results-recovery}

```{r}
# mixed logistic regressions
#
# convert factors and use effect coding
d_long$fluency <- as.factor(d_long$fluency)
d_long$quality <- as.factor(d_long$quality)
d_long$ID <- as.factor(d_long$ID)
d_long$venture <- as.factor(d_long$venture)
contrasts(d_long$fluency) <- contr.sum # high = 1, low = -1
contrasts(d_long$quality) <- contr.sum # high = 1, low = -1

# answers to valid decks per condition
d_rec_control <- d_long |> filter(condition == "control" & !is.na(recovery_correct))
d_rec_disclosure <- d_long |> filter(condition == "disclosure" & !is.na(recovery_correct))
d_rec_explanation <- d_long |> filter(condition == "disclosure_explanation" & !is.na(recovery_correct))

# control condition (exploratory)
m_rec_control <- lme4::glmer(recovery_correct ~ fluency + quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                             data = d_rec_control,
                             family = binomial,
                             control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
# disclosure condition (preregistered)
m_rec_disclosure <- lme4::glmer(recovery_correct ~ fluency + quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                                data = d_rec_disclosure,
                                family = binomial,
                                control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
# disclosure plus explanation condition (exploratory)
m_rec_explanation <- lme4::glmer(recovery_correct ~ fluency + quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                                 data = d_rec_explanation,
                                 family = binomial,
                                 control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

# observed share of correct answers and fluency effect per condition
bind_rows(
  recovery_tbl(m_rec_control, d_rec_control$recovery_correct, d_rec_control$fluency),
  recovery_tbl(m_rec_disclosure, d_rec_disclosure$recovery_correct, d_rec_disclosure$fluency),
  recovery_tbl(m_rec_explanation, d_rec_explanation$recovery_correct, d_rec_explanation$fluency)
) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Outcome", "Fluency Condition", "N", "% Correct", "z-test", "p (two-sided)", "Odds Ratio (High vs. Low)"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  pack_rows(index = c("Control (Exploratory)" = 2, "Disclosure (Preregistered)" = 2,
                      "Disclosure + Explanation (Exploratory)" = 2),
            label_row_css = "text-align: center;")
```

::: {.table-note style="font-size: 80%; text-align: left;"}
*Notes:* Test statistics, p-values (two-sided), and odds ratios (high vs. low fluency, i.e., exp(2 × coefficient)) from mixed logistic regressions per condition with visual fluency and substantive quality as predictors and random intercepts for participants and startups. The models are based on `r scales::comma(nobs(m_rec_control))` answers from `r lme4::ngrps(m_rec_control)[["ID"]]` participants (control), `r scales::comma(nobs(m_rec_disclosure))` answers from `r lme4::ngrps(m_rec_disclosure)[["ID"]]` participants (disclosure), and `r scales::comma(nobs(m_rec_explanation))` answers from `r lme4::ngrps(m_rec_explanation)[["ID"]]` participants (disclosure plus explanation), each across `r lme4::ngrps(m_rec_disclosure)[["venture"]]` startups.
:::

Factual recovery
:::

### Investment allocation

As preregistered, we computed the fluency contrast on the allocated units (i.e., the mean units of the two high fluency decks minus the mean units of the two low fluency decks) and tested it against zero in the control condition (one-sided, positive) and in the disclosure condition (two-sided). Since the preregistration considered the allocation too noisy for an equivalence test at this sample size, a non-significant estimate in the disclosure condition should be interpreted as such, not as evidence that the effect is absent. @tbl-results-allocation shows the results, together with the (exploratory) test in the disclosure plus explanation condition.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-results-allocation
#| tbl-cap: 'One-sample t-tests of the fluency contrast on the investment allocation (in units out of 100)'

# fluency contrast (allocation) per condition
allocation_control <- d_valid$fluency_contrast_allocation[d_valid$condition == "control"]
allocation_disclosure <- d_valid$fluency_contrast_allocation[d_valid$condition == "disclosure"]
allocation_explanation <- d_valid$fluency_contrast_allocation[d_valid$condition == "disclosure_explanation"]

# --Note: control one-sided (positive), the other conditions two-sided
temp <- bind_rows(
  contrast_tbl(allocation_control, alternative = "greater"),
  contrast_tbl(allocation_disclosure, alternative = "two.sided"),
  contrast_tbl(allocation_explanation, alternative = "two.sided")
)
temp$p_one_sided <- c(temp$p[1], NA, NA)
temp$p_two_sided <- c(NA, temp$p[2], temp$p[3])
temp |>
  mutate(Condition = c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure + explanation"),
         Test = c("Preregistered", "Preregistered", "Exploratory")) |>
  select(Condition, Test, N, Mean, SD, CI, test_statistic, p_one_sided, p_two_sided, d) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Condition", "Test", "N", "Mean", "SD", "95% CI", "t-test", "p (one-sided)", "p (two-sided)", "Cohen's d<sub>z</sub>"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(c(6, 7), extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

### Belief check

After the investment allocation, participants indicated how much the visual design of the decks had told them about the startups' quality (belief item 1) and about their founders' competence (belief item 2), from 1 = nothing at all to 7 = a great deal. As preregistered, we tested whether disclosure lowered the belief that the design was informative about the startups' quality, using a Welch t-test on belief item 1 (disclosure vs. control, one-sided, disclosure lower). A signaling interpretation of the result in the disclosure condition requires that disclosure lowered this belief. If the test is not significant, the fluency estimate is reported, but the signaling test is inconclusive. In addition, we compared belief item 2 between the disclosure and the control condition with a Welch t-test (two-sided). This second test was not preregistered and is exploratory. For consistency with the confirmatory tests, we used the analyzable sample. @tbl-results-belief-1 shows the mean beliefs per condition, and @tbl-results-belief-2 shows the results of the two tests.

::: {#tbl-results-belief layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-results-belief-1}

```{r}
# mean beliefs per condition
d_valid |> group_by(condition) |>
  summarize(N = n(), m_quality = mean(belief_quality), sd_quality = sd(belief_quality),
            m_founders = mean(belief_founders), sd_founders = sd(belief_founders)) |>
  mutate(condition = c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure + explanation")) |>
  kbl(digits = 2, col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Mean", "SD")) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Item 1: Venture Quality" = 2, "Item 2: Founders' Competence" = 2))
```

Mean beliefs per condition
:::

::: {#tbl-results-belief-2}

```{r}
# belief check (Welch t-tests, disclosure vs. control)

#         item 2 exploratory (two-sided)
belief_control <- d_valid$belief_quality[d_valid$condition == "control"]
belief_disclosure <- d_valid$belief_quality[d_valid$condition == "disclosure"]
belief_founders_control <- d_valid$belief_founders[d_valid$condition == "control"]
belief_founders_disclosure <- d_valid$belief_founders[d_valid$condition == "disclosure"]

temp <- bind_rows(
  welch_tbl(belief_disclosure, belief_control, alternative = "less"),
  welch_tbl(belief_founders_disclosure, belief_founders_control, alternative = "two.sided")
)
temp$p_one_sided <- c(temp$p[1], NA)
temp$p_two_sided <- c(NA, temp$p[2])
temp |>
  mutate(Item = c("Item 1: Venture quality", "Item 2: Founders' competence"),
         Test = c("Preregistered", "Exploratory")) |>
  select(Item, Test, N_1, N_2, Mean_1, Mean_2, test_statistic, p_one_sided, p_two_sided, d) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Belief Item", "Test", "N (Disclosure)", "N (Control)", "Mean (Disclosure)", "Mean (Control)", "t-test",
                    "p (one-sided)", "p (two-sided)", "Cohen's d"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(7, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

## Manipulation checks {#sec-mc}

In this section, we report the results of the manipulation checks for visual fluency and substantive quality. As preregistered, they use the control condition only. At the end of the experiment, participants rated each deck with respect to how easy it had been to study the pitch deck (processing ease, from 0 = difficult to 100 = easy) and the startup's potential irrespective of the pitch deck's visual design (perceived venture quality, from 1 = very poor to 7 = excellent). Since the observation-level exclusions only apply to the deck-level dependent variables, the manipulation checks use all decks of all participants in the control condition.

As preregistered, we estimated two mixed-effects models, one that predicts processing ease by visual fluency and one that predicts perceived venture quality by substantive quality, both with random intercepts for participants and startups and with effect coding (i.e., `low` as `-1` and `high` as `+1`). For processing ease and perceived venture quality, @tbl-results-mc-1 and @tbl-results-mc-2 show the observed (i.e., not model-based) mean ratings per condition, together with the test of the respective factor in the mixed-effects model (Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom) and a standardized effect size.

::: {#tbl-results-mc layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-results-mc-1}

```{r}
# control condition only (as preregistered)
d_long_control <- d_long |> filter(condition == "control")

# mixed-effects models
#
# processing ease (called felt ease in the preregistration; 0-100 slider)
m_mc_fluency <- lmerTest::lmer(ease ~ fluency + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture), d_long_control)
# perceived quality (1-7 scale), all decks
m_mc_quality <- lmerTest::lmer(rating_all ~ quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture), d_long_control)

# processing ease
mc_tbl(m_mc_fluency, "fluency1", d_long_control$ease, d_long_control$fluency, "Processing ease") |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Outcome", "Fluency Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "t-test", "p (two-sided)", "Cohen's d"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(6, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

Processing ease
:::

::: {#tbl-results-mc-2}

```{r}
# perceived quality
mc_tbl(m_mc_quality, "quality1", d_long_control$rating_all, d_long_control$quality, "Perceived venture quality") |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Outcome", "Quality Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "t-test", "p (two-sided)", "Cohen's d"),
      escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(6, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

::: {.table-note style="font-size: 80%; text-align: left;"}
*Notes:* Test statistics, p-values (two-sided), and effect sizes from mixed-effects models with random intercepts for participants and startups (`r scales::comma(nobs(m_mc_fluency))` ratings from `r lme4::ngrps(m_mc_fluency)[["ID"]]` participants across `r lme4::ngrps(m_mc_fluency)[["venture"]]` startups per model). Cohen's d is the model-based difference between the high and the low condition, divided by the square root of the sum of the variance components (Westfall et al., 2014).
:::

Perceived venture quality
:::

Manipulation checks (control condition)

The model-based difference is thus `r sprintf('%.2f', 2 * lme4::fixef(m_mc_fluency)["fluency1"])` rating points for processing ease and `r sprintf('%.2f', 2 * lme4::fixef(m_mc_quality)["quality1"])` rating points for perceived quality.

## Sensitivity analyses {#sec-sensitivity}

As preregistered, we re-estimated the analyses of the disclosure condition (a) excluding participants who needed all three attempts to answer the comprehension questions about their instruction message (including those who failed all three attempts), and (b) excluding participants who answered anything other than "No" to the question whether they had formed a guess about what we were testing. In the analyzable sample, `r sum(d_valid$comprehension_attempts == 3)` participants needed three attempts (control: `r sum(d_valid$comprehension_attempts[d_valid$condition == "control"] == 3)`; disclosure: `r sum(d_valid$comprehension_attempts[d_valid$condition == "disclosure"] == 3)`; disclosure plus explanation: `r sum(d_valid$comprehension_attempts[d_valid$condition == "disclosure_explanation"] == 3)`), and `r sum(d_valid$suspicion_probe != "No")` participants answered *Yes* or *Maybe a little* to the question whether they had formed a guess. The exclusions were applied to all conditions, so that the comparison of the control and the disclosure condition in the decision rule uses the same reduced sample. @tbl-results-sensitivity shows the results for the disclosure condition, next to the results for the full analyzable sample.

::: {#tbl-results-sensitivity}

```{r}
# (a) excluding participants who needed all three instruction attempts
d_sens_1 <- d_valid |> filter(comprehension_attempts < 3)
sens_1_control <- d_sens_1$fluency_contrast_rating[d_sens_1$condition == "control"]
sens_1_disclosure <- d_sens_1$fluency_contrast_rating[d_sens_1$condition == "disclosure"]
# (b) excluding participants who reported a hypothesis guess
d_sens_2 <- d_valid |> filter(suspicion_probe == "No")
sens_2_control <- d_sens_2$fluency_contrast_rating[d_sens_2$condition == "control"]
sens_2_disclosure <- d_sens_2$fluency_contrast_rating[d_sens_2$condition == "disclosure"]

# estimate, 95% CI, Bayes factor, equivalence test, comparison with the control
# condition, and decision rule
#
# full analyzable sample
bf_full <- BayesFactor::extractBF(BayesFactor::ttestBF(x = contrast_disclosure, mu = 0, rscale = 0.707))$bf
ci95_full <- t.test(contrast_disclosure)$conf.int
ci90_full <- t.test(contrast_disclosure, conf.level = .90)$conf.int
p_zero_full <- t.test(contrast_disclosure)$p.value
p_comp_full <- t.test(contrast_control, contrast_disclosure, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value
# (a)
bf_sens_1 <- BayesFactor::extractBF(BayesFactor::ttestBF(x = sens_1_disclosure, mu = 0, rscale = 0.707))$bf
ci95_sens_1 <- t.test(sens_1_disclosure)$conf.int
ci90_sens_1 <- t.test(sens_1_disclosure, conf.level = .90)$conf.int
p_zero_sens_1 <- t.test(sens_1_disclosure)$p.value
p_comp_sens_1 <- t.test(sens_1_control, sens_1_disclosure, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value
# (b)
bf_sens_2 <- BayesFactor::extractBF(BayesFactor::ttestBF(x = sens_2_disclosure, mu = 0, rscale = 0.707))$bf
ci95_sens_2 <- t.test(sens_2_disclosure)$conf.int
ci90_sens_2 <- t.test(sens_2_disclosure, conf.level = .90)$conf.int
p_zero_sens_2 <- t.test(sens_2_disclosure)$p.value
# decision rule
decision_sens_1 <- h2_decision(sens_1_disclosure, sens_1_control)
decision_sens_2 <- h2_decision(sens_2_disclosure, sens_2_control)
p_comp_sens_2 <- t.test(sens_2_control, sens_2_disclosure, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value

data.frame(
  Sample = c("Full analyzable sample", "(a) Without participants who needed three instruction attempts",
             "(b) Without participants who reported a hypothesis guess"),
  N = c(length(contrast_disclosure), length(sens_1_disclosure), length(sens_2_disclosure)),
  Mean = weights::rd(c(mean(contrast_disclosure), mean(sens_1_disclosure), mean(sens_2_disclosure)), 2),
  CI95 = c(paste0("[", weights::rd(ci95_full[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(ci95_full[2], 2), "]"),
           paste0("[", weights::rd(ci95_sens_1[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(ci95_sens_1[2], 2), "]"),
           paste0("[", weights::rd(ci95_sens_2[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(ci95_sens_2[2], 2), "]")),
  p_zero = ifelse(c(p_zero_full, p_zero_sens_1, p_zero_sens_2) < .001, " &lt; .001",
                  weights::rd(c(p_zero_full, p_zero_sens_1, p_zero_sens_2), 3)),
  BF = bf_fmt(c(bf_full, bf_sens_1, bf_sens_2)),
  CI90 = c(paste0("[", weights::rd(ci90_full[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(ci90_full[2], 2), "]"),
           paste0("[", weights::rd(ci90_sens_1[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(ci90_sens_1[2], 2), "]"),
           paste0("[", weights::rd(ci90_sens_2[1], 2), ", ", weights::rd(ci90_sens_2[2], 2), "]")),
  Equivalence = ifelse(c(ci90_full[1] > -eq_bound & ci90_full[2] < eq_bound,
                         ci90_sens_1[1] > -eq_bound & ci90_sens_1[2] < eq_bound,
                         ci90_sens_2[1] > -eq_bound & ci90_sens_2[2] < eq_bound), "yes", "no"),
  p_comp = weights::rd(c(p_comp_full, p_comp_sens_1, p_comp_sens_2), 3),
  Decision = paste0("Case ", h2_step(c(decision_h2, decision_sens_1, decision_sens_2)),
                    " (", h2_outcome(c(decision_h2, decision_sens_1, decision_sens_2)), ")")
) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("Sample", "N", "Mean", "95% CI", "p (two-sided)", "BF<sub>10</sub>", "90% CI", "Equivalence",
                    "p (Control vs. Disclosure, two-sided)", "Decision Rule"),
      escape = FALSE, align = "lccccccccc") |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(c(4, 7), extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;")
```

::: {.table-note style="font-size: 80%; text-align: left;"}
*Notes:* Interpretation of BF<sub>10</sub> (classification of Lee & Wagenmakers, 2013): `r bf_label(bf_full)` in the full analyzable sample, `r bf_label(bf_sens_1)` in (a), and `r bf_label(bf_sens_2)` in (b).
:::

Sensitivity analyses: Fluency contrast (in rating points) in the disclosure condition
:::


## Exploratory analyses {#sec-exploratory}

As preregistered, we explored (a) the fluency × quality interaction on the quality ratings and on the allocated units, including whether the added explanation (disclosure plus explanation vs. disclosure) changes it, and (b) order and position effects. Since no directions were preregistered, all tests are two-sided. All models are mixed-effects models with random intercepts for participants and startups, the factors are effect-coded (i.e., `low` as `-1` and `high` as `+1`; for the comparison of the two disclosure conditions, `disclosure` as `+1` and `disclosure_explanation` as `-1`; for the halves, `first` as `+1` and `second` as `-1`; for the sequences, `hq_first` (high quality decks first) as `+1` and `lq_first` as `-1`), and invalid decks are not included. With effect coding, the coefficient of a two-way interaction is a quarter of the corresponding difference of differences (e.g., the fluency effect at high quality minus the fluency effect at low quality), and the coefficient of a three-way interaction is an eighth of the corresponding difference (e.g., this difference of differences in the disclosure condition minus that in the disclosure plus explanation condition). The tables therefore also report these differences (i.e., four or eight times the coefficient) with their 95% confidence intervals, as well as the number of observations and participants of each model.

@tbl-results-interaction shows the fluency × quality interactions per condition and the three-way interaction that tests whether the fluency × quality interaction differs between the two disclosure conditions, for the quality ratings (@tbl-results-interaction-1) and for the allocated units (@tbl-results-interaction-2). The models for the allocated units have a singular fit: since the allocations of every participant add up to 100, the participant intercepts have a variance of zero. The fixed effects are not affected by this.

::: {#tbl-results-interaction layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-results-interaction-1}

```{r}
# data for the comparison of the two disclosure conditions (effect coding)
d_long_act <- d_long |> filter(condition %in% c("disclosure", "disclosure_explanation")) |>
  mutate(condition = droplevels(condition))
contrasts(d_long_act$condition) <- contr.sum # disclosure = 1, disclosure_explanation = -1

# quality ratings: mixed-effects models
m_int_rating_control <- lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ fluency * quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                                       d_long |> filter(condition == "control"))
m_int_rating_disclosure <- lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ fluency * quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                                          d_long |> filter(condition == "disclosure"))
m_int_rating_explanation <- lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ fluency * quality + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                                           d_long |> filter(condition == "disclosure_explanation"))
m_int_rating_act <- lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ fluency * quality * condition + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                                   d_long_act)

# row labels and column names of the tables
terms_int <- c("Fluency × quality (control)", "Fluency × quality (disclosure)",
               "Fluency × quality (disclosure + explanation)",
               "Fluency × quality × condition (disclosure vs. disclosure + explanation)")
cols_int <- c("", "Coeff.", "SE", "Difference", "95% CI", "t-test", "p (two-sided)", "Observations", "Participants")

# quality ratings: table
# --Note: difference = 4 x coefficient (two-way) or 8 x coefficient (three-way)
bind_rows(
  lmer_coef_tbl(m_int_rating_control, "fluency1:quality1", multiplier = 4, coef_digits = 3),
  lmer_coef_tbl(m_int_rating_disclosure, "fluency1:quality1", multiplier = 4, coef_digits = 3),
  lmer_coef_tbl(m_int_rating_explanation, "fluency1:quality1", multiplier = 4, coef_digits = 3),
  lmer_coef_tbl(m_int_rating_act, "fluency1:quality1:condition1", multiplier = 8, coef_digits = 3)
) |>
  mutate(term = terms_int) |>
  select(term, estimate, std.error, difference, ci, test_statistic, p, observations, participants) |>
  kbl(col.names = cols_int, escape = FALSE, align = "lcccccccc") |>
  kable_styling() |>
  column_spec(c(5, 6), extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;") |>
  row_spec(c(0,3), extra_css = "border-bottom: 1px solid")
```

Quality ratings (1–7)

:::

Exploratory analysis: Fluency × quality interactions (mixed-effects models)
:::

@tbl-results-order shows the order and position effects on the quality ratings. First, we tested whether the quality rating depends on the position in which a deck was viewed (1–4) or on the position of its rating page (1–4), controlling for fluency and quality (all conditions; positions as factors; type III tests with Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom; @tbl-results-order-1). Second, we tested whether the fluency effect differs between the decks viewed before and after the midway reminder (per condition, since the reminder differed between the conditions) and between the two rotation sequences (i.e., high quality decks first vs. low quality decks first; all conditions; @tbl-results-order-2). Here, the column `Difference` is the fluency effect in the first half minus that in the second half (or in the sequence with the high quality decks first minus that in the sequence with the low quality decks first).

::: {#tbl-results-order layout-nrow=2}

::: {#tbl-results-order-1}

```{r}
# convert factors and use effect coding
d_long$half <- as.factor(d_long$half)
d_long$sequence <- as.factor(d_long$sequence)
contrasts(d_long$half) <- contr.sum     # first = 1, second = -1
contrasts(d_long$sequence) <- contr.sum # hq_first = 1, lq_first = -1

# (a) position effects (all conditions)
m_position <- lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ fluency + quality + factor(position) +
                               factor(rating_position) + (1 | ID) + (1 | venture),
                             d_long)
temp <- anova(m_position)[c("factor(position)", "factor(rating_position)"), ]
data.frame(
  term = c("Viewing position of the deck (1–4)", "Position of the rating page (1–4)"),
  test_statistic = paste0("F(", temp$NumDF, ", ", sprintf('%.1f', temp$DenDF), ") = ", sprintf('%.2f', temp$`F value`)),
  p = ifelse(temp$`Pr(>F)` < .001, " &lt; .001", weights::rd(temp$`Pr(>F)`, 3))
) |>
  kbl(col.names = c("", "F-test", "p"), escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling()
```

# Plots {#sec-plots}

@fig-main summarizes the key results: for each instruction condition, it shows the fluency contrasts on the perceived venture quality ratings and on the investment allocation, together with the mean beliefs about the informativeness of the design (belief check). @fig-contrast shows the fluency contrast on the perceived venture quality ratings by condition in detail, including the preregistered equivalence bounds, and @fig-decision shows which case of the preregistered decision rule for the disclosure condition an estimate would yield. @fig-ratings shows the mean quality ratings per condition and experimental cell, where significance brackets represent post-hoc contrasts (two-sided paired t-tests) with Holm (1979) correction, and @fig-recovery shows the results for factual recovery.

```{r}
#| label: fig-main
#| fig-cap: Fluency contrasts and beliefs by instruction condition
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| out-width: 100%

# Helper functions and aesthetics
#
# pval function
pval <- function(p, stars = TRUE){
  if(stars){
    if(p < .001) return("***")
    if(p < .01) return("**")
    if(p < .05) return("*")
    if(p >= .05) return("NS")
  } else{
    scales::pvalue(p, prefix = c("p < ", "p = ", "p > "))
  }
}
#
# mean and 95% CI of a participant-level contrast, put together as a data frame
contrast_ci <- function(x, panel, group){
  # remove missing values
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  # perform (two-sided) t-test
  tres <- t.test(x, mu = 0)
  # construct return df
  return(data.frame(panel = panel, group = group, estimate = mean(x),
                    lower = tres$conf.int[1], upper = tres$conf.int[2]))
}
# theme settings
my_style <- list(hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc(),
                 scale_fill_manual(values=c(blue_light, blue_dark)))
my_theme <- theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, hjust = .5, margin = margin(t = 0, r = 10, b = 0, l = 0)),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, hjust = .5, margin = margin(t = 5, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)),
        )


# data prep
#
# panel titles and groups
panels_contrast <- c("<b>Perceived venture quality</b><br><span style='color:gray45'>rating points (1–7 scale)</span>",
                     "<b>Allocation</b><br><span style='color:gray45'>units out of 100</span>")
groups <- c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure +\nexplanation")

# means and 95% CIs of the fluency contrasts
d_ci <- bind_rows(
  # perceived quality ratings
  contrast_ci(contrast_control, panels_contrast[1], groups[1]),
  contrast_ci(contrast_disclosure, panels_contrast[1], groups[2]),
  contrast_ci(contrast_explanation, panels_contrast[1], groups[3]),
  # allocation
  contrast_ci(allocation_control, panels_contrast[2], groups[1]),
  contrast_ci(allocation_disclosure, panels_contrast[2], groups[2]),
  contrast_ci(allocation_explanation, panels_contrast[2], groups[3])
)
d_ci$panel <- factor(d_ci$panel, levels = panels_contrast)
d_ci$group <- factor(d_ci$group, levels = groups)
# means and 95% CIs of the belief that the design is informative about the
# startups' quality
panel_belief <- "<b>Design informative about quality</b><br><span style='color:gray45'>mean belief (1–7 scale)</span>"
d_ci_belief <- bind_rows(
  contrast_ci(d_valid$belief_quality[d_valid$condition == "control"], panel_belief, groups[1]),
  contrast_ci(d_valid$belief_quality[d_valid$condition == "disclosure"], panel_belief, groups[2]),
  contrast_ci(d_valid$belief_quality[d_valid$condition == "disclosure_explanation"], panel_belief, groups[3])
)
d_ci_belief$group <- factor(d_ci_belief$group, levels = groups)

# preregistered equivalence bounds (only in the panel for the perceived quality ratings)
d_band <- data.frame(panel = factor(panels_contrast[1], levels = panels_contrast), ymin = -eq_bound, ymax = eq_bound)

# figure: fluency contrasts
main_1 <- ggplot(d_ci, aes(x = group, y = estimate)) +
  geom_rect(data = d_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
            fill = "gray85", alpha = .6, color = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray45", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .1, linewidth = .9, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", estimate)), nudge_x = .14, hjust = 0, size = 3.8,
            color = "gray25", family = "Roboto Condensed") +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(.4, .6))) +
  hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc() + my_theme +
  theme(strip.text = element_markdown(size = 11, hjust = .5, lineheight = 1.2),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5),
        plot.title = element_markdown(size = 13, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain", hjust = 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fluency contrast",
       title = "<b>Fluency contrast</b> (high minus low fluency decks)")

# figure: beliefs
main_2 <- ggplot(d_ci_belief, aes(x = group, y = estimate)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .1, linewidth = .9, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", estimate)), nudge_x = .14, hjust = 0, size = 3.8,
            color = "gray25", family = "Roboto Condensed") +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(.4, .6))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc() + my_theme +
  theme(strip.text = element_markdown(size = 11, hjust = .5, lineheight = 1.2),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5),
        plot.title = element_markdown(size = 13, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain", hjust = 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean belief",
       title = "<b>Belief check</b>")

# final (combined) figure
main_1 + main_2 + plot_layout(widths = c(2.3, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
  title = "<b>Fluency contrasts and beliefs by instruction condition</b>",
  subtitle = "Means and 95% confidence intervals (Study 4)",
  caption = paste0("<i>Notes:</i><br>", "The gray band marks the preregistered equivalence bounds for the disclosure condition (±", eq_bound, " rating points). ",
                   "Analyzable sample (n = ", nrow(d_valid), " participants with four valid decks)."),
  # --Note: `theme` inside `plot_annotation`, so that the titles of the two
  #         parts keep their (smaller) size
  theme = theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(size = 18, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, family = "Roboto Condensed"),
    plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_markdown(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2, family = "Roboto Condensed", size = 10, margin = margin(t = 7, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-contrast
#| fig-cap: Fluency contrast on the quality ratings by instruction condition, with the preregistered equivalence bounds
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| out-width: 100%

# data prep
#
# for convenience and to not interfere with later code, we work on a copy of
# the data
d_contrast <- d_valid
d_contrast$condition <- factor(d_contrast$condition,
                               levels = c("control", "disclosure", "disclosure_explanation"),
                               labels = c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure +\nexplanation"))
# means, 95% CIs, and 90% CIs per condition
d_est <- d_contrast |> group_by(condition) |>
  summarize(mean = mean(fluency_contrast_rating),
            lower_95 = t.test(fluency_contrast_rating)$conf.int[1],
            upper_95 = t.test(fluency_contrast_rating)$conf.int[2],
            lower_90 = t.test(fluency_contrast_rating, conf.level = .90)$conf.int[1],
            upper_90 = t.test(fluency_contrast_rating, conf.level = .90)$conf.int[2])

# labels that include statistical inference
p_h1 <- t.test(contrast_control, alternative = "greater")$p.value
p_comp <- t.test(contrast_control, contrast_disclosure, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value
p_h3 <- t.test(contrast_disclosure, contrast_explanation, alternative = "greater", var.equal = FALSE)$p.value
d_est$label <- c(paste0("p", ifelse(p_h1 < .001, " &lt; .001", paste0(" = ", weights::rd(p_h1, 3))), "<br>(one-sided, > 0)"),
                 paste0("decision rule:<br>case ", h2_step(decision_h2)),
                 "")

# participants with the same contrast are placed side by side (like a dot
# plot) instead of jittering them; the width of a row is proportional to its
# number of participants (widest row = .8 units)
d_contrast <- d_contrast |> group_by(condition, fluency_contrast_rating) |>
  mutate(n_tied = n(), rank_tied = row_number()) |> ungroup()
d_contrast$x_dot <- as.numeric(d_contrast$condition) +
  (d_contrast$rank_tied - (d_contrast$n_tied + 1) / 2) / max(d_contrast$n_tied) * .8

# figure: participant-level contrasts
contrast_1 <- ggplot(d_contrast, aes(x = x_dot, y = fluency_contrast_rating)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -eq_bound, ymax = eq_bound,
           fill = "gray85", alpha = .6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray45", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_point(color = "gray40", size = 1.1, alpha = .3, stroke = 0) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = as.numeric(condition)), color = blue_dark, geom = "errorbar",
               fun.data = mean_cl_normal, width = .15, linewidth = 1.1) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = as.numeric(condition)), color = blue_dark, geom = "point", fun = mean, size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = levels(d_contrast$condition)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-4, 4, 2)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(.5, 3.5)) +
  hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc() + my_theme +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fluency contrast (rating points)",
       title = "<b>Individual participants</b><br>
       <span style='color:gray45; font-size:12pt'>(one dot per participant; means with 95% CIs)</span>") +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown(face = "plain"))

# figure: estimates with 95% and 90% CIs (zoomed)
contrast_2 <- ggplot(d_est, aes(x = condition, y = mean)) +
  # --Note: `geom_blank()` first, so that the x-axis is discrete
  geom_blank() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -eq_bound, ymax = eq_bound,
           fill = "gray85", alpha = .6) +
  annotate("text", x = .5, y = c(-eq_bound, eq_bound), label = c(paste0("-", eq_bound), paste0("+", eq_bound)),
           hjust = 0, vjust = c(1.4, -.6), size = 3.5, color = "gray35", family = "Roboto Condensed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray45", linewidth = .4) +
  # 90% CI (thick) and 95% CI (thin)
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower_90, ymax = upper_90), linewidth = 3, color = blue_main, alpha = .6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95), width = .1, linewidth = .9, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_richtext(aes(label = label), nudge_x = .12, hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "gray25",
                fill = NA, label.color = NA, family = "Roboto Condensed", lineheight = 1.2) +
  geom_signif(
    # control vs. disclosure (two-sided)
    xmin = 1, xmax = 2, y_position = .88, tip_length = .01,
    annotations = paste0("p = ", weights::rd(p_comp, 3), " (two-sided)"),
    color = "gray45", vjust = -.5, textsize = 3.5, family = "Roboto Condensed"
  ) +
  geom_signif(
    # disclosure vs. disclosure plus explanation (one-sided)
    xmin = 2, xmax = 3, y_position = .68, tip_length = .01,
    annotations = paste0("p = ", weights::rd(p_h3, 3), " (one-sided)"),
    color = "gray45", vjust = -.5, textsize = 3.5, family = "Roboto Condensed"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-.2, 1, .2)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-.3, 1.12)) +
  hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc() + my_theme +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fluency contrast (rating points)",
       title = "<b>Estimates and equivalence bounds</b><br>
       <span style='color:gray45; font-size:12pt'>(means with 95% CIs and 90% CIs)</span>") +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown(face = "plain"))

# final (combined) figure
contrast_1 + contrast_2 +
  plot_annotation(
  title = "<b>Preregistered fluency contrast on the perceived venture quality ratings</b>",
  subtitle = "Difference between the high and the low fluency decks, by instruction condition (Study 4)",
  caption = paste0("<i>Notes:</i><br>", "The gray band marks the preregistered equivalence bounds for the disclosure condition (±", eq_bound, " rating points).<br>",
                   "Right: thin error bars indicate 95% CIs, thick bars 90% CIs ",
                   "(equivalence requires the 90% CI to lie inside the bounds). ",
                   "n = ", nrow(d_valid), " participants with four valid decks."),
) & theme(
  plot.title = element_markdown(size = 18, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain"),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, family = "Roboto Condensed"),
  plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_markdown(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2, family = "Roboto Condensed", size = 10, margin = margin(t = 7, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)),
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-decision
#| fig-cap: Preregistered decision rule for the disclosure condition as a function of the estimate
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: 0.5
#| out-width: 100%

# data prep
#
# step of the preregistered decision rule for hypothetical estimates of the
# fluency contrast in the disclosure condition, holding the standard deviation
# and the sample size of the disclosure condition and the data of the control
# condition at their observed values (i.e., the tests of `h2_decision`,
# computed for a grid of estimates)
n_disc <- length(contrast_disclosure)
se_disc <- sd(contrast_disclosure) / sqrt(n_disc)
grid <- data.frame(estimate = seq(-.6, .6, by = .001))
# two-sided test against zero
grid$p_zero <- 2 * pt(-abs(grid$estimate / se_disc), df = n_disc - 1)
grid$sig_negative <- grid$p_zero < .05 & grid$estimate < 0
grid$sig_positive <- grid$p_zero < .05 & grid$estimate > 0
# equivalence test (TOST)
grid$p_lower <- pt((grid$estimate + eq_bound) / se_disc, df = n_disc - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
grid$p_upper <- pt((grid$estimate - eq_bound) / se_disc, df = n_disc - 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
grid$equivalence <- grid$p_lower < .05 & grid$p_upper < .05
# control vs. disclosure (Welch t-test, two-sided): control effect higher?
var_ctrl <- var(contrast_control) / length(contrast_control)
var_disc <- var(contrast_disclosure) / n_disc
df_welch <- (var_ctrl + var_disc)^2 /
  (var_ctrl^2 / (length(contrast_control) - 1) + var_disc^2 / (n_disc - 1))
grid$p_comparison <- 2 * pt(-abs((mean(contrast_control) - grid$estimate) / sqrt(var_ctrl + var_disc)), df = df_welch)
grid$control_higher <- grid$p_comparison < .05 & mean(contrast_control) > grid$estimate
# decision rule (steps in the preregistered order)
grid$step <- dplyr::case_when(
  grid$sig_negative & grid$estimate <= -eq_bound ~ 1,
  grid$sig_positive & grid$estimate >= eq_bound ~ 2,
  grid$equivalence & grid$control_higher ~ 3,
  grid$sig_positive & grid$estimate < eq_bound & !grid$equivalence ~ 4,
  TRUE ~ 5)
# consecutive grid points with the same step form one segment
grid$segment <- cumsum(c(1, diff(grid$step) != 0))
d_steps <- grid |> group_by(segment, step) |>
  summarize(xmin = max(min(estimate) - .0005, -.6), xmax = min(max(estimate) + .0005, .6)) |> ungroup()
d_steps$step <- factor(d_steps$step, levels = 1:5,
                       labels = c("1: overcorrection", "2: persistence supported",
                                  "3: switched off", "4: reduced but present", "5: indeterminate"))
# observed estimate with its 95% and 90% CIs
ci95_disc <- t.test(contrast_disclosure)$conf.int
ci90_disc <- t.test(contrast_disclosure, conf.level = .90)$conf.int
d_obs <- data.frame(estimate = mean(contrast_disclosure),
                    lower_95 = ci95_disc[1], upper_95 = ci95_disc[2],
                    lower_90 = ci90_disc[1], upper_90 = ci90_disc[2])
# step at the observed estimate (as a check, the same step as `h2_decision`)
step_observed <- grid$step[which.min(abs(grid$estimate - d_obs$estimate))]

# plot
ggplot() +
  # steps of the decision rule (upper row)
  geom_rect(data = d_steps, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 1.75, ymax = 2.45, fill = step)) +
  geom_text(data = d_steps, aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = 2.1, label = as.integer(step)),
            color = "white", size = 4.5, family = "Roboto Condensed", fontface = "bold") +
  # equivalence bounds and zero
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-eq_bound, eq_bound), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray35", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray45", linewidth = .4) +
  annotate("text", x = c(-eq_bound, eq_bound), y = .5, label = c(paste0("-", eq_bound), paste0("+", eq_bound)),
           hjust = c(1.1, -.1), size = 3.5, color = "gray35", family = "Roboto Condensed") +
  # observed estimate (lower row): 90% CI (thick) and 95% CI (thin)
  geom_linerange(data = d_obs, aes(y = 1, xmin = lower_90, xmax = upper_90), linewidth = 3, color = blue_main, alpha = .6) +
  geom_errorbar(data = d_obs, aes(y = 1, xmin = lower_95, xmax = upper_95), orientation = "y",
                width = .15, linewidth = .9, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_point(data = d_obs, aes(x = estimate, y = 1), size = 3.5, color = blue_dark) +
  geom_text(data = d_obs, aes(x = estimate, y = 1.35, label = paste0("observed: ", sprintf('%.2f', estimate))),
            size = 3.8, color = "gray25", family = "Roboto Condensed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#D55E00", blue_dark, "#009E73", blue_main, "gray60"), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-.6, -.4, -.2, 0, .2, .4, .6), labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2.1), labels = c("Observed\nestimate", "Case of the\ndecision rule")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-.6, .6), ylim = c(.4, 2.5)) +
  hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc() + my_theme +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 10.5),
        plot.title = element_markdown(size = 18, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain", hjust = 0),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, family = "Roboto Condensed", hjust = 0),
        plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_markdown(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2, family = "Roboto Condensed", size = 10,
                                    margin = margin(t = 7, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Fluency contrast in the disclosure condition (rating points)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "<b>Preregistered decision rule for the disclosure condition</b>",
       subtitle = "Case that an estimate would yield, given the observed standard error and the control condition (Study 4)",
       caption = paste0("<i>Notes:</i><br>", "The dashed lines mark the preregistered equivalence bounds (±", eq_bound, " rating points). ",
                        "Observed estimate: thin error bar = 95% CI, thick bar = 90% CI (n = ", n_disc, ").<br>",
                        "Cases were computed with the same tests as the decision rule, holding the standard deviation and n of the disclosure condition<br>",
                        "and the control condition fixed. The observed estimate falls into case ", step_observed, "."))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ratings
#| fig-cap: Perceived venture quality ratings by visual fluency and substantive quality in the three instruction conditions
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| out-width: 100%

# set up titles, axis names etc.
my_labs <- labs(
  x = "Quality",
  fill = "Fluency"
)

# data prep
#
# for convenience and to not interfere with later code, we work on a copy of
# the data (analyzable sample)
d_rat <- d_long_valid
# convert fluency and quality to factor vars
d_rat$fluency <- factor(d_rat$fluency, levels = c("low", "high"), labels = c("Low", "High"))
d_rat$quality <- factor(d_rat$quality, levels = c("low", "high"), labels = c("Low", "High"))
d_rat_ctrl <- d_rat |> filter(condition == "control")
d_rat_disc <- d_rat |> filter(condition == "disclosure")
d_rat_expl <- d_rat |> filter(condition == "disclosure_explanation")
d_ctrl <- d_valid |> filter(condition == "control")
d_disc <- d_valid |> filter(condition == "disclosure")
d_expl <- d_valid |> filter(condition == "disclosure_explanation")

# cell means and upper CI bounds (needed for label and bracket positions)
sum_ctrl <- d_rat_ctrl |> group_by(quality, fluency) |>
  summarize(mean = mean(rating), upper = ggplot2::mean_cl_normal(rating)$ymax)
sum_disc <- d_rat_disc |> group_by(quality, fluency) |>
  summarize(mean = mean(rating), upper = ggplot2::mean_cl_normal(rating)$ymax)
sum_expl <- d_rat_expl |> group_by(quality, fluency) |>
  summarize(mean = mean(rating), upper = ggplot2::mean_cl_normal(rating)$ymax)
# --Note: The significance brackets are placed 0.24 rating points (i.e., 4% of
#         the 1-7 axis) above the upper CI bound.


# FIGURE FOR THE CONTROL CONDITION
#
# post-hoc contrasts: high vs. low fluency within each quality level
# (paired t-tests on the wide data, Holm's correction)
p_lq <- t.test(d_ctrl$rating_lq_hf, d_ctrl$rating_lq_lf, paired = TRUE)$p.value
p_hq <- t.test(d_ctrl$rating_hq_hf, d_ctrl$rating_hq_lf, paired = TRUE)$p.value
temp <- p.adjust(c(p_lq, p_hq), method = "holm")

# contrast: low quality: high vs. low fluency
p1 <- temp[1]
# contrast: high quality: high vs. low fluency
p2 <- temp[2]

# plot
rating_1 <- ggplot(d_rat_ctrl, aes(x=quality, y=rating, fill=fluency)) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom="bar", position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom="errorbar", width=.08, linewidth=.9,
               position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  # cell means as labels inside the bars
  geom_text(data = sum_ctrl,
            aes(x = quality, y = 1.2, label = sprintf("%.2f", mean), group = fluency,
                color = fluency),
            position = position_dodge(.91), vjust = 0, size = 3.8,
            family = "Roboto Condensed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray15", "white"), guide = "none") +
  my_style + my_theme + my_labs +
  labs(y = "Perceived venture quality (1–7)",
       title = paste0("<b>Control</b><br>
         <span style='color:gray45; font-size:12pt'>(n = ", nrow(d_ctrl), ")</span>")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown(face = "plain")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +
  geom_signif(
    # p1
    xmin = c(0.775), xmax = c(1.225),
    y_position = max(sum_ctrl$upper[sum_ctrl$quality == "Low"]) + .24,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p1),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
    ) +
  geom_signif(
    # p2
    xmin = c(1.775), xmax = c(2.225),
    y_position = max(sum_ctrl$upper[sum_ctrl$quality == "High"]) + .24,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p2),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
  )


# FIGURE FOR THE DISCLOSURE CONDITION
#
# post-hoc contrasts: high vs. low fluency within each quality level
# (paired t-tests on the wide data, Holm's correction)
p_lq <- t.test(d_disc$rating_lq_hf, d_disc$rating_lq_lf, paired = TRUE)$p.value
p_hq <- t.test(d_disc$rating_hq_hf, d_disc$rating_hq_lf, paired = TRUE)$p.value
temp <- p.adjust(c(p_lq, p_hq), method = "holm")

# contrast: low quality: high vs. low fluency
p1 <- temp[1]
# contrast: high quality: high vs. low fluency
p2 <- temp[2]

# plot
rating_2 <- ggplot(d_rat_disc, aes(x=quality, y=rating, fill=fluency)) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom="bar", position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom="errorbar", width=.08, linewidth=.9,
               position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  # cell means as labels inside the bars
  geom_text(data = sum_disc,
            aes(x = quality, y = 1.2, label = sprintf("%.2f", mean), group = fluency,
                color = fluency),
            position = position_dodge(.91), vjust = 0, size = 3.8,
            family = "Roboto Condensed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray15", "white"), guide = "none") +
  my_style + my_theme + my_labs +
  labs(y = "Perceived venture quality (1–7)",
       title = paste0("<b>Disclosure</b><br>
         <span style='color:gray45; font-size:12pt'>(n = ", nrow(d_disc), ")</span>")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown(face = "plain")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +
  geom_signif(
    # p1
    xmin = c(0.775), xmax = c(1.225),
    y_position = max(sum_disc$upper[sum_disc$quality == "Low"]) + .24,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p1),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
    ) +
  geom_signif(
    # p2
    xmin = c(1.775), xmax = c(2.225),
    y_position = max(sum_disc$upper[sum_disc$quality == "High"]) + .24,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p2),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
  )


# FIGURE FOR THE DISCLOSURE PLUS EXPLANATION CONDITION
#
# post-hoc contrasts: high vs. low fluency within each quality level
# (paired t-tests on the wide data, Holm's correction)
p_lq <- t.test(d_expl$rating_lq_hf, d_expl$rating_lq_lf, paired = TRUE)$p.value
p_hq <- t.test(d_expl$rating_hq_hf, d_expl$rating_hq_lf, paired = TRUE)$p.value
temp <- p.adjust(c(p_lq, p_hq), method = "holm")

# contrast: low quality: high vs. low fluency
p1 <- temp[1]
# contrast: high quality: high vs. low fluency
p2 <- temp[2]

# plot
rating_3 <- ggplot(d_rat_expl, aes(x=quality, y=rating, fill=fluency)) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom="bar", position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom="errorbar", width=.08, linewidth=.9,
               position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  # cell means as labels inside the bars
  geom_text(data = sum_expl,
            aes(x = quality, y = 1.2, label = sprintf("%.2f", mean), group = fluency,
                color = fluency),
            position = position_dodge(.91), vjust = 0, size = 3.8,
            family = "Roboto Condensed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray15", "white"), guide = "none") +
  my_style + my_theme + my_labs +
  labs(y = "Perceived venture quality (1–7)",
       title = paste0("<b>Disclosure + explanation</b><br>
         <span style='color:gray45; font-size:12pt'>(n = ", nrow(d_expl), ")</span>")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown(face = "plain")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +
  geom_signif(
    # p1
    xmin = c(0.775), xmax = c(1.225),
    y_position = max(sum_expl$upper[sum_expl$quality == "Low"]) + .24,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p1),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
    ) +
  geom_signif(
    # p2
    xmin = c(1.775), xmax = c(2.225),
    y_position = max(sum_expl$upper[sum_expl$quality == "High"]) + .24,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p2),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
  )


# final (combined) figure
rating_1 + rating_2 + rating_3 + plot_layout(guides = 'collect') +
  plot_annotation(
  title = "<b>Perceived venture quality of the four pitch decks in the three instruction conditions</b>",
  subtitle = "as a function of quality and fluency (Study 4)",
  caption = paste0("<i>Notes:</i><br>", "Error bars indicate 95% confidence intervals around the mean. ",
                   "Significance brackets represent post-hoc contrasts (two-sided paired t-tests) with Holm (1979) correction.<br>",
                   "n = ", nrow(d_valid), " participants with four valid decks.")
) & theme(
  plot.title = element_markdown(size = 18, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain"),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, family = "Roboto Condensed"),
  plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_markdown(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2, family = "Roboto Condensed", size = 10, margin = margin(t = 7, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)),
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-recovery
#| fig-cap: Factual recovery by visual fluency and instruction condition
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| out-width: 100%

# data prep
#
# for convenience and to not interfere with later code, we work on a copy of
# the data
# --Note: For the plot, we compute each participant's share of correct answers
#         across the two decks per fluency level (invalid decks are not
#         included). The inference statistics stem from the mixed logistic
#         regressions (see above).
d_rec <- d_long |> filter(!is.na(recovery_correct))
d_rec$fluency <- factor(d_rec$fluency, levels = c("low", "high"), labels = c("Low", "High"))
d_rec$condition <- factor(d_rec$condition, levels = c("control", "disclosure", "disclosure_explanation"),
                          labels = c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure +\nexplanation"))
rec_fluency <- d_rec |> group_by(ID, condition, fluency) |>
  summarize(value = mean(recovery_correct)) |> ungroup()

# labels that include statistical inference (odds ratios of the fluency effect)
str_rec <- c(paste0("OR = ", sprintf('%.2f', exp(2 * lme4::fixef(m_rec_control)["fluency1"]))),
             paste0("OR = ", sprintf('%.2f', exp(2 * lme4::fixef(m_rec_disclosure)["fluency1"]))),
             paste0("OR = ", sprintf('%.2f', exp(2 * lme4::fixef(m_rec_explanation)["fluency1"]))))
d_labels_rec <- data.frame(condition = factor(c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure +\nexplanation"),
                                              levels = c("Control", "Disclosure", "Disclosure +\nexplanation")),
                           label = str_rec)

# means and upper CI bounds per condition and fluency level (needed for the
# labels inside the bars and the bracket positions)
sum_rec <- rec_fluency |> group_by(condition, fluency) |>
  summarize(mean = mean(value), upper = ggplot2::mean_cl_normal(value)$ymax)
# p-values of the fluency effects
p_rec_ctrl <- coef(summary(m_rec_control))["fluency1", "Pr(>|z|)"]
p_rec_disc <- coef(summary(m_rec_disclosure))["fluency1", "Pr(>|z|)"]
p_rec_expl <- coef(summary(m_rec_explanation))["fluency1", "Pr(>|z|)"]

# plot
ggplot(rec_fluency, aes(x=condition, y=value, fill=fluency)) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom="bar", position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom="errorbar", width=.08, linewidth=.9,
               position=position_dodge(.91)) +
  # means as labels inside the bars
  geom_text(data = sum_rec,
            aes(x = condition, y = .055, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean), group = fluency,
                color = fluency),
            position = position_dodge(.91), vjust = 0, size = 4.2,
            family = "Roboto Condensed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray15", "white"), guide = "none") +
  geom_text(data = d_labels_rec, aes(x = condition, y = .98, label = label),
            size = 3.8, color = "gray25", family = "Roboto Condensed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  my_style + my_theme +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Correct answers", fill = "Fluency",
       title = "<b>Factual recovery by fluency and instruction condition</b>",
       subtitle = "Share of correct answers to the factual questions (Study 4)",
       caption = paste0("<i>Notes:</i><br>", "Error bars indicate 95% confidence intervals around the mean of the participants' shares of correct answers.<br>",
                        "Odds ratios (OR; high vs. low fluency) and significance brackets from mixed logistic regressions ",
                        "with participant and startup random intercepts<br>(two-sided; preregistered test: disclosure condition). ",
                        "n = ", length(unique(rec_fluency$ID)), " participants with at least one valid deck.")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown(size = 18, family = "Roboto Condensed", face = "plain", hjust = 0),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, family = "Roboto Condensed", hjust = 0),
        plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_markdown(hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.2, family = "Roboto Condensed", size = 10,
                                    margin = margin(t = 7, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0))) +
  geom_signif(
    # control condition: high vs. low fluency
    xmin = c(0.775), xmax = c(1.225),
    y_position = max(sum_rec$upper[sum_rec$condition == "Control"]) + .03,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p_rec_ctrl),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
    ) +
  geom_signif(
    # disclosure condition: high vs. low fluency
    xmin = c(1.775), xmax = c(2.225),
    y_position = max(sum_rec$upper[sum_rec$condition == "Disclosure"]) + .03,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p_rec_disc),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
    ) +
  geom_signif(
    # disclosure plus explanation condition: high vs. low fluency
    xmin = c(2.775), xmax = c(3.225),
    y_position = max(sum_rec$upper[sum_rec$condition == "Disclosure +\nexplanation"]) + .03,
    tip_length = .003,
    annotations = pval(p_rec_expl),
    color = "gray45",
    vjust = .0
  )
```
